It has been said: this is the Qur'an, for the establishment of the two Books is not valid without establishing it. It is also possible that what is meant is what was sent down to them through the tongues of the prophets other than the two Books.

His words: ﴿And surely what has been sent down to you from your Lord will increase many of them in transgression and disbelief﴾: that is, disbelief added to their disbelief and transgression added to their transgression. What is meant by "many of them" is those who did not become Muslim and persisted in obstinacy. It has also been said that what is meant is their scholars. The opening of this sentence with an oath is to emphasize its content. His words: ﴿So do not grieve over the disbelieving people﴾: that is, leave off grieving over these people, for the harm of that returns to them and descends upon them, and among those who follow you from the believers there is sufficiency for you in place of them. His words: (﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾) and so on, is a resumed sentence to encourage those among the believers other than them.

What is meant by "the believers" here are those who believed with their tongues, and they are the hypocrites. (﴿And those who became Jews﴾): that is, those who entered the religion of the Jews. (And the Sabians): it is in the nominative by way of inception, and its predicate is omitted; the estimated meaning is: "and the Sabians and the Christians likewise." Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: the nominative is taken as having been placed out of order, and the estimated meaning is: "Indeed, those who believed and those who became Jews, whoever believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteous deeds, there is no fear for them nor will they grieve, and the Sabians and the Christians likewise." Sibawayh recited the verse of the poet:

"Otherwise, know that we and you are transgressors as long as we remain in schism."

That is: otherwise, know that we are transgressors and you likewise. Similar to it is the saying of Dabi al-Burjumi:

"Whoever has his dwelling in Medina by evening, then I and Qayyar in it are strangers."

That is: then I am a stranger, and Qayyar likewise. Al-Kisa'i and al-Akhfash said: (al-Sabi'un) is in conjunction with the pronoun in (hadu). Al-Nahhas said: I heard al-Zajjaj say, when the saying of al-Kisa'i and al-Akhfash was mentioned to him: "This is an error for two reasons: first, a pronoun in the nominative is not conjoined to unless it is emphasized. Second, the conjoined is a partner of the conjoined-to, so the meaning becomes: the Sabians have entered Judaism, and this is absurd."

Al-Farra' said: the nominative was permitted because "inna" is weak, so it affects only the subject and not the predicate. Thus, according to him, it is conjoined to the position (mahall) of the subject of inna, or to the whole of inna and its subject. It has also been said: the predicate of inna is omitted, and the following clause is the predicate of al-Sabi'un and al-Nasara, as in the saying of the poet:

"We are with what we have, and you are with what you have pleased, and opinions differ."

It has also been said: "inna" here means "na'am" (yes), so al-Sabi'un is in the nominative by inception, and similar to it is the saying of Qays ibn al-Ruqayyat:

"The blamers began in youth, so they blame me and I blame them,
And they say, 'Gray hair has risen over you, and you have grown old,' so I said, 'Innah.'"

Al-Akhfash said: "innah" means "na'am," and the ha' is for pausal (silence). The discussion of the Sabians and the Christians has already passed in al-Baqarah. It was read as al-Sabiyun with a clear ya', to ease the hamza, and it was read as al-Sabun without a ya'; it is from sabā yaṣbū, because they inclined (ṣabaw) toward following desire. (p-386) It was also read as wal-Sabi'in, in conjunction with the noun of inna.

His words: (﴿whoever believed in Allah﴾) is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿then no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾, and the subject with its predicate is the predicate of inna. The entry of the fa' is because the subject includes the meaning of a condition. The returning pronoun to the noun of inna is omitted; that is, whoever among them believed. It is also possible that "whoever believed" is a substitute for the noun of inna and what is conjoined to it, and the predicate of inna is "then no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve." The meaning, on the supposition that what is meant by "those who believed" are the hypocrites, as we have mentioned, is that whoever among these groups believed with sincere faith in the required manner and did righteous deeds, he is the one upon whom there is no fear nor grief. As for the supposition that what is meant by "those who believed" is all the people of Islam, both the sincere and the hypocrite, then what is meant by "whoever believed" is one who is characterized by sincere faith and persists in it, and whoever brings about sincere faith after his hypocrisy.

His words: ﴿Certainly We took the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾: a new statement to explain some of their vile deeds. The meaning of the covenant (mithaq) has already been explained in al-Baqarah. (﴿And We sent to them messengers﴾) to inform them of the laws and to warn them. (﴿Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire﴾): a conditional sentence which came as an answer to the question of some of the rabbis about the sending of the messengers, as if it was said: "What did they do with the messengers?" The answer of the condition is omitted; that is: they disobeyed him.

His words: ﴿a group they denied, and a group they kill﴾ is also a resumed sentence, an answer to the question of some people about the first answer, as if it was said: "How did they treat them?" So it was said: a group of them denied them and did not harm them, and another group of them killed them. He said "and a group they kill" only for the sake of observing the rhyme endings of the verses. Among those they denied were Jesus and similar prophets, and among those they killed were Zechariah and John (Yahya). His words: ﴿And they thought there would be no trial﴾: that is, those upon whom Allah had taken the covenant thought that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would not send trial and testing through hardships, being deceived by their saying: ﴿We are the sons of Allah and His beloved﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 18]. Abu 'Amr, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read (takun) with the nominative, on the basis that "an" is the lightened form of the heavy (an), and hasiba is in the sense of "knew," because "an" means confirmation. The rest read it with the accusative, on the basis that "an" is governing the verb, and hasiba is in the sense of "supposed." Al-Nahhas said: The nominative in hasibat and its sisters is better according to the grammarians, and similar to it is:

"Has not Basbasa claimed today that I have grown old, and that those like me should not witness the play?"

His words: ﴿so they became blind and deaf﴾: that is, they became blind to seeing guidance, and deaf to hearing the truth. This is a reference to what occurred from the Children of Israel at the beginning of disobeying the rulings of the Torah and the killing of Sha'ya. Then Allah relented toward them when they repented, and He removed the famine from them. ﴿Then they became blind and deaf, many of them﴾. This is a reference to what occurred from them after repentance, of the killing of Yahya ibn Zakariyya and their intent to kill Jesus. The word "many" (kathir) is in the nominative as a substitute for the pronoun in the two verbs. Al-Akhfash said: as you say, "I saw your people, all three of them," and if you wish it can be by supposing an implied subject; that is: the blind and the deaf, many of them. It is also possible that "many" is nominative as subject, according to the dialect of one who says: "The fleas ate me" (akalunī al-barāghīth), and from it is the saying of the poet:

"But rather, a Dafafi whose father and mother
In Hawran press sesame oil, are his relatives."

It was also read as ('umu wa-summu), in the passive voice; that is, Allah made them blind and deaf. His words: ﴿Certainly those who said: Indeed Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary, have disbelieved﴾: this is a new statement containing an explanation of some of the disgraceful acts of the People of the Book. The ones who uttered this saying are a sect among them, called the Ya'qubiyya; it has also been said they are the Malkaniyya. They said: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, indwelt the essence of Jesus. So Allah refuted them with His saying: ﴿And the Messiah said: O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord﴾; that is: and the situation is that the Messiah himself said this saying, so how can they claim divinity for one who acknowledges against himself that he is a servant like them? His words: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise﴾: the pronoun is for the matter (ash-shan), and this is a new statement containing an explanation that associating partners with Allah makes the entry into Paradise forbidden. It has also been said it is from the saying of Jesus: ﴿and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers﴾, who would help them so that they enter Paradise, or rescue them from the Fire.

His words: ﴿Certainly those who said: Indeed Allah is the third of three have disbelieved﴾: this is also a new statement to explain some of their disgraceful acts. What is meant by "third of three" is one of three, and for this reason it is annexed to what follows it, and tanwin is not permitted, as al-Zajjaj and others said. It is only given tanwin and what follows it is put in the accusative when what follows it is one rank below it, like "third of two" and "fourth of three." The ones who said that He, glorified and exalted, is the third of three are the Christians, and what is meant by the three is: Allah, glorified is He, Jesus, and Mary, as indicated by His saying: ﴿Did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116]. This is what is meant by the saying: three hypostases (aqanim): the hypostasis of the Father, the hypostasis of the Son, and the hypostasis of the Holy Spirit. A discussion of this has already passed in Surat al-Nisa'. Then Allah, glorified is He, refuted their false claim, saying: ﴿And there is no god except One God﴾; that is: there is no existence except Allah, glorified is He. This sentence is circumstantial, and the meaning is: they said that saying while the situation is that nothing exists except Allah. The "min" in His saying "min ilah" is for emphasizing the comprehensiveness derived from the negation. ﴿And if they do not desist from what they say﴾ of disbelief, ﴿a painful punishment will surely befall those of them who disbelieved﴾: the answer to an implied oath, which takes the place of the answer of the condition. The "min" in "minhum" is explanatory or partitive. ﴿Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness?﴾ The fa' is for conjunction with an implied element, and the hamza is for denunciation.

His words: ﴿The Messiah, son of Mary, was only a messenger; messengers had passed away before him﴾: that is, he is confined to the messengership and does not go beyond it, as you claim. The clause ﴿messengers had passed away before him﴾ is a qualifier of "messenger"; that is: he is only a messenger of the kind of the messengers who passed away before him. The miracles that occurred through him do not necessitate that he is a god, for those before him had similar ones. Allah brought the staff to life in Moses' hand, and created Adam without a father. How then do you make the reviving of the dead by Jesus and his existence without a father necessitate that he is a god? If he were a god for that reason, then the messengers before him who brought the like of what he brought would be gods, and you do not say that.

His words: (﴿And his mother was a truthful woman﴾) is conjoined to the Messiah; that is: and his mother was only a truthful woman, that is, truthful in what she says, or one who affirms what her son brought of messengership. That does not require divinity for her; rather she is like any other woman characterized by this description. His words: (p-387) ﴿They both used to eat food﴾: a resumed statement containing confirmation of what was indicated, that they are like the rest of mankind; that is: whoever eats food as created beings do is not a lord, but rather a servant who is lorded over, born of women. So when is he fit to be a lord?! As for your saying that he ate food by his humanity (nasut) and not by his divinity (lahut), this is a false statement that implies the mixing of God with what is not God, and the combining of humanity and divinity. If it were permissible for the eternal to mix with the temporal, it would be permissible for the eternal to be temporal, and if this were valid regarding Jesus, it would be valid regarding other servants. ﴿Look how We make the signs clear for them﴾: that is, the proofs. In this is an expression of wonder at the state of those who make those attributes necessitate divinity, while overlooking that they exist in one whom they do not claim to be a god. (﴿Then look how they are turned away﴾): that is, how are they turned away from the truth after this clarification? It is said: "afakahu yafikuhu" when he turned him away. He repeated the command to look for emphasis in expressing wonder, and he used "then" (thumma) to show the disparity between the two wonders.

Al-Shawkani, *Fath al-Qadir*, commentary on Surah al-Ma'idah (5), verses 68–76 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Nafi' ibn Harithah, Sallam ibn Mishkam, Malik ibn al-Sayf and Rafi' ibn Harmalah came and said: 'O Muhammad, do you not claim that you are upon the religion (millah) and creed of Ibrahim, and that you believe in what we have of the Torah and testify that it is true from Allah?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Yes, but you have introduced innovations, denied what is in it of the covenant that was taken from you, and concealed from it what you were commanded to make clear to the people. So I am free of your innovations.' They said: 'Indeed we are held accountable for what is in our hands, we are upon guidance and truth, and we will not believe in you or follow you.' So Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Say: O People of the Book, you are not upon anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel﴾, up to His saying: ﴿the disbelieving people﴾."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Hasan regarding His saying: ﴿And they thought there would be no trial﴾ that he said: "It is affliction (bala')."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah a similar statement. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi a statement similar to it.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Certainly those who said, "Allah is the third of three," have disbelieved﴾ that he said: "The Christians say, 'Allah is the third of three,' and they have lied."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, who said: "The Children of Israel split into three groups regarding 'Isa. One group said: 'He is Allah.' Another group said: 'He is the son of Allah.' And another group said: 'He is the servant of Allah and His spirit.' The last of these is the moderate one (al-muqtasidah), and they are the Muslims among the People of the Book."

His words: ﴿And surely what has been sent down to you from your Lord will increase many of them in transgression and disbelief﴾: that is, disbelief added to their disbelief and transgression added to their transgression. What is meant by "many of them" is those who did not become Muslim and persisted in obstinacy. It has also been said that what is meant is their scholars. The opening of this sentence with an oath is to emphasize its content. His words: ﴿So do not grieve over the disbelieving people﴾: that is, leave off grieving over these people, for the harm of that returns to them and descends upon them, and among those who follow you from the believers there is sufficiency for you in place of them. His words: (﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾) and so on, is a resumed sentence to encourage those among the believers other than them.

What is meant by "the believers" here are those who believed with their tongues, and they are the hypocrites. (﴿And those who became Jews﴾): that is, those who entered the religion of the Jews. (And the Sabians): it is in the nominative by way of inception, and its predicate is omitted; the estimated meaning is: "and the Sabians and the Christians likewise." Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: the nominative is taken as having been placed out of order, and the estimated meaning is: "Indeed, those who believed and those who became Jews, whoever believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteous deeds, there is no fear for them nor will they grieve, and the Sabians and the Christians likewise." Sibawayh recited the verse of the poet:

"Otherwise, know that we and you are transgressors as long as we remain in schism."

That is: otherwise, know that we are transgressors and you likewise. Similar to it is the saying of Dabi al-Burjumi:

"Whoever has his dwelling in Medina by evening, then I and Qayyar in it are strangers."

That is: then I am a stranger, and Qayyar likewise. Al-Kisa'i and al-Akhfash said: (al-Sabi'un) is in conjunction with the pronoun in (hadu). Al-Nahhas said: I heard al-Zajjaj say, when the saying of al-Kisa'i and al-Akhfash was mentioned to him: "This is an error for two reasons: first, a pronoun in the nominative is not conjoined to unless it is emphasized. Al-Farra' said: the nominative was permitted because "inna" is weak, so it affects only the subject and not the predicate. Thus, according to him, it is conjoined to the position (mahall) of the subject of inna, or to the whole of inna and its subject. It has also been said: the predicate of inna is omitted, and the following clause is the predicate of al-Sabi'un and al-Nasara, as in the saying of the poet:

"We are with what we have, and you are with what you have pleased, and opinions differ."

It has also been said: "inna" here means "na'am" (yes), so al-Sabi'un is in the nominative by inception, and similar to it is the saying of Qays ibn al-Ruqayyat:

"The blamers began in youth, so they blame me and I blame them,
And they say, 'Gray hair has risen over you, and you have grown old,' so I said, 'Innah.'"

Al-Akhfash said: "innah" means "na'am," and the ha' is for pausal (silence). The discussion of the Sabians and the Christians has already passed in al-Baqarah. It was read as al-Sabiyun with a clear ya', to ease the hamza, and it was read as al-Sabun without a ya'; it is from sabā yaṣbū, because they inclined (ṣabaw) toward following desire. (p-386) It was also read as wal-Sabi'in, in conjunction with the noun of inna.

His words: (﴿whoever believed in Allah﴾) is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿then no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾, and the subject with its predicate is the predicate of inna. The entry of the fa' is because the subject includes the meaning of a condition. The returning pronoun to the noun of inna is omitted; that is, whoever among them believed. It is also possible that "whoever believed" is a substitute for the noun of inna and what is conjoined to it, and the predicate of inna is "then no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve." The meaning, on the supposition that what is meant by "those who believed" are the hypocrites, as we have mentioned, is that whoever among these groups believed with sincere faith in the required manner and did righteous deeds, he is the one upon whom there is no fear nor grief. As for the supposition that what is meant by "those who believed" is all the people of Islam, both the sincere and the hypocrite, then what is meant by "whoever believed" is one who is characterized by sincere faith and persists in it, and whoever brings about sincere faith after his hypocrisy.

His words: ﴿Certainly We took the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾: a new statement to explain some of their vile deeds. The meaning of the covenant (mithaq) has already been explained in al-Baqarah. (﴿And We sent to them messengers﴾) to inform them of the laws and to warn them. (﴿Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire﴾): a conditional sentence which came as an answer to the question of some of the rabbis about the sending of the messengers, as if it was said: "What did they do with the messengers?" The answer of the condition is omitted; that is: they disobeyed him.

His words: ﴿a group they denied, and a group they kill﴾ is also a resumed sentence, an answer to the question of some people about the first answer, as if it was said: "How did they treat them?" So it was said: a group of them denied them and did not harm them, and another group of them killed them. He said "and a group they kill" only for the sake of observing the rhyme endings of the verses. Among those they denied were Jesus and similar prophets, and among those they killed were Zechariah and John (Yahya). His words: ﴿And they thought there would be no trial﴾: that is, those upon whom Allah had taken the covenant thought that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would not send trial and testing through hardships, being deceived by their saying: ﴿We are the sons of Allah and His beloved﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 18]. Abu 'Amr, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read (takun) with the nominative, on the basis that "an" is the lightened form of the heavy (an), and hasiba is in the sense of "knew," because "an" means confirmation. The rest read it with the accusative, on the basis that "an" is governing the verb, and hasiba is in the sense of "supposed." Al-Nahhas said: The nominative in hasibat and its sisters is better according to the grammarians, and similar to it is:

"Has not Basbasa claimed today that I have grown old, and that those like me should not witness the play?"

His words: ﴿so they became blind and deaf﴾: that is, they became blind to seeing guidance, and deaf to hearing the truth. This is a reference to what occurred from the Children of Israel at the beginning of disobeying the rulings of the Torah and the killing of Sha'ya. Then Allah relented toward them when they repented, and He removed the famine from them. ﴿Then they became blind and deaf, many of them﴾. This is a reference to what occurred from them after repentance, of the killing of Yahya ibn Zakariyya and their intent to kill Jesus. The word "many" (kathir) is in the nominative as a substitute for the pronoun in the two verbs. Al-Akhfash said: as you say, "I saw your people, all three of them," and if you wish it can be by supposing an implied subject; that is: the blind and the deaf, many of them. It is also possible that "many" is nominative as subject, according to the dialect of one who says: "The fleas ate me" (akalunī al-barāghīth), and from it is the saying of the poet:

"But rather, a Dafafi whose father and mother
In Hawran press sesame oil, are his relatives."

It was also read as ('umu wa-summu), in the passive voice; that is, Allah made them blind and deaf. His words: ﴿Certainly those who said: Indeed Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary, have disbelieved﴾: this is a new statement containing an explanation of some of the disgraceful acts of the People of the Book. The ones who uttered this saying are a sect among them, called the Ya'qubiyya; it has also been said they are the Malkaniyya. They said: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, indwelt the essence of Jesus. So Allah refuted them with His saying: ﴿And the Messiah said: O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord﴾; that is: and the situation is that the Messiah himself said this saying, so how can they claim divinity for one who acknowledges against himself that he is a servant like them? His words: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise﴾: the pronoun is for the matter (ash-shan), and this is a new statement containing an explanation that associating partners with Allah makes the entry into Paradise forbidden. It has also been said it is from the saying of Jesus: ﴿and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers﴾, who would help them so that they enter Paradise, or rescue them from the Fire.

His words: ﴿Certainly those who said: Indeed Allah is the third of three have disbelieved﴾: this is also a new statement to explain some of their disgraceful acts. What is meant by "third of three" is one of three, and for this reason it is annexed to what follows it, and tanwin is not permitted, as al-Zajjaj and others said. It is only given tanwin and what follows it is put in the accusative when what follows it is one rank below it, like "third of two" and "fourth of three." The ones who said that He, glorified and exalted, is the third of three are the Christians, and what is meant by the three is: Allah, glorified is He, Jesus, and Mary, as indicated by His saying: ﴿Did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116]. This is what is meant by the saying: three hypostases (aqanim): the hypostasis of the Father, the hypostasis of the Son, and the hypostasis of the Holy Spirit. A discussion of this has already passed in Surat al-Nisa'. Then Allah, glorified is He, refuted their false claim, saying: ﴿And there is no god except One God﴾; that is: there is no existence except Allah, glorified is He. This sentence is circumstantial, and the meaning is: they said that saying while the situation is that nothing exists except Allah. The "min" in His saying "min ilah" is for emphasizing the comprehensiveness derived from the negation. ﴿And if they do not desist from what they say﴾ of disbelief, ﴿a painful punishment will surely befall those of them who disbelieved﴾: the answer to an implied oath, which takes the place of the answer of the condition. The "min" in "minhum" is explanatory or partitive. ﴿Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness?﴾ The fa' is for conjunction with an implied element, and the hamza is for denunciation.

His words: ﴿The Messiah, son of Mary, was only a messenger; messengers had passed away before him﴾: that is, he is confined to the messengership and does not go beyond it, as you claim. The clause ﴿messengers had passed away before him﴾ is a qualifier of "messenger"; that is: he is only a messenger of the kind of the messengers who passed away before him. The miracles that occurred through him do not necessitate that he is a god, for those before him had similar ones. Allah brought the staff to life in Moses' hand, and created Adam without a father. How then do you make the reviving of the dead by Jesus and his existence without a father necessitate that he is a god? If he were a god for that reason, then the messengers before him who brought the like of what he brought would be gods, and you do not say that.

His words: (﴿And his mother was a truthful woman﴾) is conjoined to the Messiah; that is: and his mother was only a truthful woman, that is, truthful in what she says, or one who affirms what her son brought of messengership. That does not require divinity for her; rather she is like any other woman characterized by this description. His words: (p-387) ﴿They both used to eat food﴾: a resumed statement containing confirmation of what was indicated, that they are like the rest of mankind; that is: whoever eats food as created beings do is not a lord, but rather a servant who is lorded over, born of women. So when is he fit to be a lord?! The ones who said that He, glorified and exalted, is the third of three are the Christians, and what is meant by the three is: Allah, glorified is He, Jesus, and Mary, as indicated by His saying: ﴿Did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116]. This is what is meant by the saying: three hypostases (aqanim): the hypostasis of the Father, the hypostasis of the Son, and the hypostasis of the Holy Spirit. A discussion of this has already passed in Surat al-Nisa'. Then Allah, glorified is He, refuted their false claim, saying: ﴿And there is no god except One God﴾; that is: there is no existence except Allah, glorified is He. This sentence is circumstantial, and the meaning is: they said that saying while the situation is that nothing exists except Allah. The "min" in His saying "min ilah" is for emphasizing the comprehensiveness derived from the negation. ﴿And if they do not desist from what they say﴾ of disbelief, ﴿a painful punishment will surely befall those of them who disbelieved﴾: the answer to an implied oath, which takes the place of the answer of the condition. The "min" in "minhum" is explanatory or partitive. ﴿Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness?﴾ The fa' is for conjunction with an implied element, and the hamza is for denunciation.

His words: ﴿The Messiah, son of Mary, was only a messenger; messengers had passed away before him﴾: that is, he is confined to the messengership and does not go beyond it, as you claim. The clause ﴿messengers had passed away before him﴾ is a qualifier of "messenger"; that is: he is only a messenger of the kind of the messengers who passed away before him. The miracles that occurred through him do not necessitate that he is a god, for those before him had similar ones. Allah brought the staff to life in Moses' hand, and created Adam without a father. How then do you make the reviving of the dead by Jesus and his existence without a father necessitate that he is a god? If he were a god for that reason, then the messengers before him who brought the like of what he brought would be gods, and you do not say that.

His words: (﴿And his mother was a truthful woman﴾) is conjoined to the Messiah; that is: and his mother was only a truthful woman, that is, truthful in what she says, or one who affirms what her son brought of messengership. That does not require divinity for her; rather she is like any other woman characterized by this description. His words: (p-387) ﴿They both used to eat food﴾: a resumed statement containing confirmation of what was indicated, that they are like the rest of mankind; that is: whoever eats food as created beings do is not a lord, but rather a servant who is lorded over, born of women. So when is he fit to be a lord?! As for your saying that he ate food by his humanity (nasut) and not by his divinity (lahut), this is a false statement that implies the mixing of God with what is not God, and the combining of humanity and divinity. If it were permissible for the eternal to mix with the temporal, it would be permissible for the eternal to be temporal, and if this were valid regarding Jesus, it would be valid regarding other servants. ﴿Look how We make the signs clear for them﴾: that is, the proofs. In this is an expression of wonder at the state of those who make those attributes necessitate divinity, while overlooking that they exist in one whom they do not claim to be a god. (﴿Then look how they are turned away﴾): that is, how are they turned away from the truth after this clarification? It is said: "afakahu yafikuhu" when he turned him away. He repeated the command to look for emphasis in expressing wonder, and he used "then" (thumma) to show the disparity between the two wonders.

Al-Shawkani, *Fath al-Qadir*, commentary on Surah al-Ma'idah (5), verses 68–76 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Nafi' ibn Harithah, Sallam ibn Mishkam, Malik ibn al-Sayf and Rafi' ibn Harmalah came and said: 'O Muhammad, do you not claim that you are upon the religion (millah) and creed of Ibrahim, and that you believe in what we have of the Torah and testify that it is true from Allah?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Yes, but you have introduced innovations, denied what is in it of the covenant that was taken from you, and concealed from it what you were commanded to make clear to the people. So I am free of your innovations.' They said: 'Indeed we are held accountable for what is in our hands, we are upon guidance and truth, and we will not believe in you or follow you.' So Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Say: O People of the Book, you are not upon anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel﴾, up to His saying: ﴿the disbelieving people﴾."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Hasan regarding His saying: ﴿And they thought there would be no trial﴾ that he said: "It is affliction (bala')."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah a similar statement. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi a statement similar to it.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Certainly those who said, "Allah is the third of three," have disbelieved﴾ that he said: "The Christians say, 'Allah is the third of three,' and they have lied."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, who said: "The Children of Israel split into three groups regarding 'Isa. One group said: 'He is Allah.' Another group said: 'He is the son of Allah.' And another group said: 'He is the servant of Allah and His spirit.' The last of these is the moderate one (al-muqtasidah), and they are the Muslims among the People of the Book."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 5, verse 68–76 (part 1 of 2):

His words: (﴿on anything﴾) In this there is belittling and diminishing of what they are upon; that is: you are not upon anything worth considering until you establish the Torah and the Gospel, i.e., act upon what is in them of the commands and prohibitions of Allah, among which is your being commanded to follow Muhammad (ﷺ) and your being forbidden to oppose him. Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: It is also possible that this refers to before their abrogation (naskh) of the two. His words: "and what has been sent down to you from your Lord." It has been said: this is the Qur'an, for the establishment of the two Books is not valid without establishing it. It is also possible that what is meant is what was sent down to them through the tongues of the prophets other than the two Books.

His words: ﴿And surely what has been sent down to you from your Lord will increase many of them in transgression and disbelief﴾: that is, disbelief added to their disbelief and transgression added to their transgression. What is meant by "many of them" is those who did not become Muslim and persisted in obstinacy. It has also been said that what is meant is their scholars. The opening of this sentence with an oath is to emphasize its content. His words: ﴿So do not grieve over the disbelieving people﴾: that is, leave off grieving over these people, for the harm of that returns to them and descends upon them, and among those who follow you from the believers there is sufficiency for you in place of them. His words: (﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾) and so on, is a resumed sentence to encourage those among the believers other than them.

What is meant by "the believers" here are those who believed with their tongues, and they are the hypocrites. (﴿And those who became Jews﴾): that is, those who entered the religion of the Jews. (And the Sabians): it is in the nominative by way of inception, and its predicate is omitted; the estimated meaning is: "and the Sabians and the Christians likewise." Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: the nominative is taken as having been placed out of order, and the estimated meaning is: "Indeed, those who believed and those who became Jews, whoever believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteous deeds, there is no fear for them nor will they grieve, and the Sabians and the Christians likewise." Sibawayh recited the verse of the poet:

"Otherwise, know that we and you are transgressors as long as we remain in schism."

That is: otherwise, know that we are transgressors and you likewise. Similar to it is the saying of Dabi al-Burjumi:

"Whoever has his dwelling in Medina by evening, then I and Qayyar in it are strangers."

That is: then I am a stranger, and Qayyar likewise. Al-Kisa'i and al-Akhfash said: (al-Sabi'un) is in conjunction with the pronoun in (hadu). Al-Nahhas said: I heard al-Zajjaj say, when the saying of al-Kisa'i and al-Akhfash was mentioned to him: "This is an error for two reasons: first, a pronoun in the nominative is not conjoined to unless it is emphasized. Second, the conjoined is a partner of the conjoined-to, so the meaning becomes: the Sabians have entered Judaism, and this is absurd."

Al-Farra' said: the nominative was permitted because "inna" is weak, so it affects only the subject and not the predicate. Thus, according to him, it is conjoined to the position (mahall) of the subject of inna, or to the whole of inna and its subject. It has also been said: the predicate of inna is omitted, and the following clause is the predicate of al-Sabi'un and al-Nasara, as in the saying of the poet:

"We are with what we have, and you are with what you have pleased, and opinions differ."

It has also been said: "inna" here means "na'am" (yes), so al-Sabi'un is in the nominative by inception, and similar to it is the saying of Qays ibn al-Ruqayyat:

"The blamers began in youth, so they blame me and I blame them,
And they say, 'Gray hair has risen over you, and you have grown old,' so I said, 'Innah.'"

Al-Akhfash said: "innah" means "na'am," and the ha' is for pausal (silence). The discussion of the Sabians and the Christians has already passed in al-Baqarah. It was read as al-Sabiyun with a clear ya', to ease the hamza, and it was read as al-Sabun without a ya'; it is from sabā yaṣbū, because they inclined (ṣabaw) toward following desire. (p-386) It was also read as wal-Sabi'in, in conjunction with the noun of inna.

His words: (﴿whoever believed in Allah﴾) is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿then no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾, and the subject with its predicate is the predicate of inna. The entry of the fa' is because the subject includes the meaning of a condition. The returning pronoun to the noun of inna is omitted; that is, whoever among them believed. It is also possible that "whoever believed" is a substitute for the noun of inna and what is conjoined to it, and the predicate of inna is "then no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve." The meaning, on the supposition that what is meant by "those who believed" are the hypocrites, as we have mentioned, is that whoever among these groups believed with sincere faith in the required manner and did righteous deeds, he is the one upon whom there is no fear nor grief. As for the supposition that what is meant by "those who believed" is all the people of Islam, both the sincere and the hypocrite, then what is meant by "whoever believed" is one who is characterized by sincere faith and persists in it, and whoever brings about sincere faith after his hypocrisy.

His words: ﴿Certainly We took the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾: a new statement to explain some of their vile deeds. The meaning of the covenant (mithaq) has already been explained in al-Baqarah. (﴿And We sent to them messengers﴾) to inform them of the laws and to warn them. (﴿Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire﴾): a conditional sentence which came as an answer to the question of some of the rabbis about the sending of the messengers, as if it was said: "What did they do with the messengers?" The answer of the condition is omitted; that is: they disobeyed him.

His words: ﴿a group they denied, and a group they kill﴾ is also a resumed sentence, an answer to the question of some people about the first answer, as if it was said: "How did they treat them?" So it was said: a group of them denied them and did not harm them, and another group of them killed them. He said "and a group they kill" only for the sake of observing the rhyme endings of the verses. Among those they denied were Jesus and similar prophets, and among those they killed were Zechariah and John (Yahya). His words: ﴿And they thought there would be no trial﴾: that is, those upon whom Allah had taken the covenant thought that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would not send trial and testing through hardships, being deceived by their saying: ﴿We are the sons of Allah and His beloved﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 18]. Abu 'Amr, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read (takun) with the nominative, on the basis that "an" is the lightened form of the heavy (an), and hasiba is in the sense of "knew," because "an" means confirmation. The rest read it with the accusative, on the basis that "an" is governing the verb, and hasiba is in the sense of "supposed." Al-Nahhas said: The nominative in hasibat and its sisters is better according to the grammarians, and similar to it is:

"Has not Basbasa claimed today that I have grown old, and that those like me should not witness the play?"

His words: ﴿so they became blind and deaf﴾: that is, they became blind to seeing guidance, and deaf to hearing the truth. This is a reference to what occurred from the Children of Israel at the beginning of disobeying the rulings of the Torah and the killing of Sha'ya. Then Allah relented toward them when they repented, and He removed the famine from them. ﴿Then they became blind and deaf, many of them﴾. This is a reference to what occurred from them after repentance, of the killing of Yahya ibn Zakariyya and their intent to kill Jesus. The word "many" (kathir) is in the nominative as a substitute for the pronoun in the two verbs. Al-Akhfash said: as you say, "I saw your people, all three of them," and if you wish it can be by supposing an implied subject; that is: the blind and the deaf, many of them. It is also possible that "many" is nominative as subject, according to the dialect of one who says: "The fleas ate me" (akalunī al-barāghīth), and from it is the saying of the poet:

"But rather, a Dafafi whose father and mother
In Hawran press sesame oil, are his relatives."

It was also read as ('umu wa-summu), in the passive voice; that is, Allah made them blind and deaf. His words: ﴿Certainly those who said: Indeed Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary, have disbelieved﴾: this is a new statement containing an explanation of some of the disgraceful acts of the People of the Book. The ones who uttered this saying are a sect among them, called the Ya'qubiyya; it has also been said they are the Malkaniyya. They said: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, indwelt the essence of Jesus. So Allah refuted them with His saying: ﴿And the Messiah said: O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord﴾; that is: and the situation is that the Messiah himself said this saying, so how can they claim divinity for one who acknowledges against himself that he is a servant like them? His words: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise﴾: the pronoun is for the matter (ash-shan), and this is a new statement containing an explanation that associating partners with Allah makes the entry into Paradise forbidden. It has also been said it is from the saying of Jesus: ﴿and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers﴾, who would help them so that they enter Paradise, or rescue them from the Fire.

So I am free of your innovations.' They said: 'Indeed we are held accountable for what is in our hands, we are upon guidance and truth, and we will not believe in you or follow you.' Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Hasan regarding His saying: ﴿And they thought there would be no trial﴾ that he said: "It is affliction (bala')."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah a similar statement. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi a statement similar to it.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Certainly those who said, "Allah is the third of three," have disbelieved﴾ that he said: "The Christians say, 'Allah is the third of three,' and they have lied."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, who said: "The Children of Israel split into three groups regarding 'Isa. One group said: 'He is Allah.' Another group said: 'He is the son of Allah.' And another group said: 'He is the servant of Allah and His spirit.' The last of these is the moderate one (al-muqtasidah), and they are the Muslims among the People of the Book."

God, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, to say this statement to them as an argument against them and to cut off their doubt. That is: "Do you worship, apart from God, going beyond Him, that which possesses for you neither harm nor benefit? Rather, he is a servant who has been commanded, and whatever benefit or repelling of harm takes place at his hand is by God's empowering him and enabling him to do it. As for him, he is unable to possess for himself any of that, let alone possess it for others. And one who neither benefits nor harms, how can you take him as a god and worship him? What cause requires that?" The one meant here is the Messiah, peace be upon him. God, glorified is He, put harm before benefit, because repelling corruptions is more important than attaining benefits. (﴿But God is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾) That is: how can you worship that which possesses for you neither harm nor benefit, while God is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing? One who is such is capable of harm and benefit, since He encompasses everything heard and known, and among that are your harms and your benefits.

His saying: (﴿Do not exceed the bounds in your religion﴾). When God, glorified is He, nullified all the false doubts they relied upon, He forbade them from ghuluw (exaggeration) in their religion, which is transgressing the limit, such as affirming divinity for Jesus, as the Christians say, or belittling him from his exalted rank, as the Jews say, for all of that is blameworthy exaggeration and following the path of excess or deficiency, and choosing either of them over the path of correctness.

(Other than) is in the accusative as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun; that is: exaggeration other than the exaggeration of truth. As for exaggeration in the truth, by exerting one's full effort in searching for it and extracting its realities, it is not blameworthy. It has been said that the accusative is an exception of the connected type, and it has been said that it is an exception of the disconnected type. (﴿And do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray and went astray from the right way﴾) These are the predecessors of the People of the Book, from the two groups of the Jews and the Christians; that is, before the Muhammadan mission, upon its bearer be the best of blessings and peace. (﴿And led many astray﴾) from among the people (﴿and went astray from the right way﴾), that is, they strayed from the path of Muhammad, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, after the mission. The meaning is that their predecessors went astray before the mission and led many people astray at that time, and they went astray after the mission, either by themselves, or the straying of those whom they led astray is counted as straying for them, because they established that for them and laid down that course for them. It has been said that what is meant by the first is their disbelief in what reason requires, and by the second their disbelief in what the Law requires.

His saying: (﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed﴾), that is, God, glorified is He, cursed them (﴿by the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary﴾), that is, in the Psalms and the Gospel, by the tongue of David and Jesus, for what they did of disobedience, such as their transgression on the Sabbath and their disbelief in Jesus.

His saying: "That is because they disobeyed and transgressed" is a resumed sentence, an answer to an assumed question, and the reference of "that" is to the curse; that is: that curse was due to disobedience and transgression, not to some other cause. Then God, glorified is He, explained the disobedience and transgression with His saying: (﴿They did not forbid one another from any wrong they committed﴾), so He attributed the act to them, because its doer is one of them, even if they did not all commit it.

The meaning is: they did not forbid the disobedient one from repeating a sin he had committed, or one who was prepared to commit it. It is also possible that their description as having committed the wrong refers to the state at the time of revelation, not the state of abstaining from forbidding. The explanation of disobedience and transgression through abandoning the forbidding of wrong is because whoever neglects the obligation of forbidding wrong has disobeyed God, glorified is He, and transgressed His limits. Commanding right and forbidding wrong is among the most important Islamic principles and the most sublime of the legal obligations; for this reason, one who abandons it is a partner of the one who commits the sin and deserves the anger and vengeance of God, as happened to the People of the Sabbath. God, glorified is He, transformed those who did not join them in the act but abstained from denouncing them, just as He transformed the transgressors, and they all became apes and swine. (﴿Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart, or gives ear while he is a witness﴾) [Qaf: 37]. Then God, glorified is He, said, denouncing their failure to forbid wrong: (﴿Wretched is what they used to do﴾), that is, from their abandoning denunciation of what they were obliged to denounce.

(﴿You see many of them﴾), that is, of the Jews, like Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions, (﴿taking as allies those who disbelieved﴾), that is, the polytheists, while they are not upon their religion. (﴿Wretched is what their souls have sent forward for them﴾), that is, what their souls adorned and made attractive, or what they sent forward for their souls so that they would be repaid for it on the Day of Resurrection. The thing specified by the dispraise is (﴿that God's wrath is upon them﴾), that is, it necessitates God's wrath upon them, by omitting a modifier; or it is God's wrath upon them, by omitting a subject. It has been said that it is: that God's wrath is upon them is a substitute for "what". (﴿And if they had believed in God, the Prophet, and what was sent down to him﴾), that is, their prophet (﴿and what was revealed to him﴾) of the Book, (﴿they would not have taken them as allies﴾), that is, the polytheists; because God, glorified is He, and His Messenger sent to them, and His Book revealed to them, had all forbidden them from that. (﴿But many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾), that is, outside the guardianship of God, and outside faith in Him, His Messenger, and His Book.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "Do not exceed the bounds in your religion", he said: "Do not innovate." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Zayd, who said: "What they exaggerated in was claiming for God a consort and a son." 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "and went astray from the right way", he said: "The Jews." 'Abd al-Razzaq, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it good, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "The first thing that entered deficiency upon the Children of Israel was that a man would meet a man and say to him: 'O such-and-such, fear God and leave off what you are doing, for it is not lawful for you.' Then he would meet him the next day and that would not prevent him from being his table-companion, his drinking companion, and his sitting companion. As for exaggeration in the truth, by exerting one's full effort in searching for it and extracting its realities, it is not blameworthy. It has been said that the accusative is an exception of the connected type, and it has been said that it is an exception of the disconnected type. The thing specified by the dispraise is (﴿that God's wrath is upon them﴾), that is, it necessitates God's wrath upon them, by omitting a modifier; or it is God's wrath upon them, by omitting a subject. It has been said that it is: that God's wrath is upon them is a substitute for "what". (﴿And if they had believed in God, the Prophet, and what was sent down to him﴾), that is, their prophet (﴿and what was revealed to him﴾) of the Book, (﴿they would not have taken them as allies﴾), that is, the polytheists; because God, glorified is He, and His Messenger sent to them, and His Book revealed to them, had all forbidden them from that. (﴿But many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾), that is, outside the guardianship of God, and outside faith in Him, His Messenger, and His Book.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "Do not exceed the bounds in your religion", he said: "Do not innovate." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Zayd, who said: "What they exaggerated in was claiming for God a consort and a son." 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "and went astray from the right way", he said: "The Jews." 'Abd al-Razzaq, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it good, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "The first thing that entered deficiency upon the Children of Israel was that a man would meet a man and say to him: 'O such-and-such, fear God and leave off what you are doing, for it is not lawful for you.' Then he would meet him the next day and that would not prevent him from being his table-companion, his drinking companion, and his sitting companion. When they did that, God struck their hearts, some against others. Then He said: (﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David﴾) until His saying: (﴿defiantly disobedient﴾). Then he said: 'No, by God, you must command right and forbid wrong, and you must take hold of the hand of the wrongdoer, and you must restrain him upon the truth, restraining him firmly.'"

This hadith has been narrated through many chains, and the reports on this subject are very numerous, so we will not lengthen the discussion by mentioning them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David", he means in the Psalms, "and Jesus, son of Mary", he means in the Gospel. Abu 'Ubayd, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Abu Malik al-Ghifari regarding the verse, he said: "They were cursed by the tongue of David and so they were made apes, and by the tongue of Jesus and so they were made swine." Ibn Jarir narrated the like from Mujahid.

'Abd ibn Humayd and Abu al-Shaykh narrated the like from Qatadah. Al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws narrated from Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, traced to the Prophet: "The Children of Israel killed forty-three prophets at the beginning of the day, and a hundred and twelve men of their worshippers arose and commanded them to do right and forbade them from wrong, and they were all killed at the end of the day. They are those whom God mentioned: (﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed﴾)..." and so on.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "Wretched is what their souls have sent forward for them", he said: "What I commanded them." Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Kharaʼiti in Masawi al-Akhlaq, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, who weakened it, narrated from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, who said: "O assembly of Muslims, beware of fornication, for in it are six qualities: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in this world: the loss of radiance, the persistence of poverty, and the shortening of life. As for those in the Hereafter: God's wrath, a bad reckoning, and eternal abiding in the Fire." Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, recited: (﴿Wretched is what their souls have sent forward for them, that God's wrath is upon them, and in the punishment they will abide forever﴾).

Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir: this hadith is weak in every case. 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid regarding His saying: (﴿And if they had believed in God, the Prophet, and what was sent down to him, they would not have taken them as allies﴾), he said: "The hypocrites."

God, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, to say this statement to them as an argument against them and to cut off their doubt. That is: "Do you worship, apart from God, going beyond Him, that which possesses for you neither harm nor benefit? Rather, he is a servant who has been commanded, and whatever benefit or repelling of harm takes place at his hand is by God's empowering him and enabling him to do it. As for him, he is unable to possess for himself any of that, let alone possess it for others. And one who neither benefits nor harms, how can you take him as a god and worship him? What cause requires that?" The one meant here is the Messiah, peace be upon him. God, glorified is He, put harm before benefit, because repelling corruptions is more important than attaining benefits. (﴿But God is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾) That is: how can you worship that which possesses for you neither harm nor benefit, while God is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing? One who is such is capable of harm and benefit, since He encompasses everything heard and known, and among that are your harms and your benefits.

His saying: (﴿Do not exceed the bounds in your religion﴾). When God, glorified is He, nullified all the false doubts they relied upon, He forbade them from ghuluw (exaggeration) in their religion, which is transgressing the limit, such as affirming divinity for Jesus, as the Christians say, or belittling him from his exalted rank, as the Jews say, for all of that is blameworthy exaggeration and following the path of excess or deficiency, and choosing either of them over the path of correctness.

(Other than) is in the accusative as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun; that is: exaggeration other than the exaggeration of truth. As for exaggeration in the truth, by exerting one's full effort in searching for it and extracting its realities, it is not blameworthy. It has been said that the accusative is an exception of the connected type, and it has been said that it is an exception of the disconnected type. (﴿And do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray and went astray from the right way﴾) These are the predecessors of the People of the Book, from the two groups of the Jews and the Christians; that is, before the Muhammadan mission, upon its bearer be the best of blessings and peace. (﴿And led many astray﴾) from among the people (﴿and went astray from the right way﴾), that is, they strayed from the path of Muhammad, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, after the mission. The meaning is that their predecessors went astray before the mission and led many people astray at that time, and they went astray after the mission, either by themselves, or the straying of those whom they led astray is counted as straying for them, because they established that for them and laid down that course for them. It has been said that what is meant by the first is their disbelief in what reason requires, and by the second their disbelief in what the Law requires.

His saying: (﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed﴾), that is, God, glorified is He, cursed them (﴿by the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary﴾), that is, in the Psalms and the Gospel, by the tongue of David and Jesus, for what they did of disobedience, such as their transgression on the Sabbath and their disbelief in Jesus.

His saying: "That is because they disobeyed and transgressed" is a resumed sentence, an answer to an assumed question, and the reference of "that" is to the curse; that is: that curse was due to disobedience and transgression, not to some other cause. Then God, glorified is He, explained the disobedience and transgression with His saying: (﴿They did not forbid one another from any wrong they committed﴾), so He attributed the act to them, because its doer is one of them, even if they did not all commit it.

The meaning is: they did not forbid the disobedient one from repeating a sin he had committed, or one who was prepared to commit it. It is also possible that their description as having committed the wrong refers to the state at the time of revelation, not the state of abstaining from forbidding. The explanation of disobedience and transgression through abandoning the forbidding of wrong is because whoever neglects the obligation of forbidding wrong has disobeyed God, glorified is He, and transgressed His limits. Commanding right and forbidding wrong is among the most important Islamic principles and the most sublime of the legal obligations; for this reason, one who abandons it is a partner of the one who commits the sin and deserves the anger and vengeance of God, as happened to the People of the Sabbath. God, glorified is He, transformed those who did not join them in the act but abstained from denouncing them, just as He transformed the transgressors, and they all became apes and swine. (﴿Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart, or gives ear while he is a witness﴾) [Qaf: 37]. Then God, glorified is He, said, denouncing their failure to forbid wrong: (﴿Wretched is what they used to do﴾), that is, from their abandoning denunciation of what they were obliged to denounce.

﴿لَتَجِدَنَّ﴾ إلخ: هذه جملة مستأنفة تقرر ما فيها من تعداد مساوئ اليهود وعيوبهم، ودخول لام القسم عليها يزيدها تأكيدًا وتقريرًا. والخطاب لرسول الله (ﷺ)، أو لكل من يصلح له، كما في غير هذا الموضع من الكتاب العزيز. والمعنى في الآية: أن اليهود والمشركين، لعنهم الله، أشد جميع الناس عداوةً للمؤمنين وأصلبهم في ذلك، وأن النصارى أقرب الناس مودةً للمؤمنين. واللام في ﴿لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ في الموضعين متعلقة بمحذوف وقع صفةً لعداوةٍ ومودةٍ، وقيل هي متعلقة بعداوةٍ ومودةٍ. والإشارة بقوله: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ إلى كونهم أقرب مودةً. والباء في ﴿بِأنَّ مِنهم قِسِّيسِينَ﴾ للسببية، أي: ذلك بسبب أن منهم قسيسين، وهو جمع قِسٍّ وقِسِّيسٍ، قاله قُطرب. والقِسِّيس: العالم، وأصله من قَسَّ إذا تتبّع الشيء وطلبه. قال الراجز:

يُصْبِحْنَ عَنْ قَسِّ الأذى غَوافِلا وتَقَسَّسَتْ أصْواتُهم بِاللَّيْلِ تَسْمِعْتُها

والقَسُّ: النميمة. والقَسُّ أيضًا: رئيس النصارى في الدين والعلم، وجمعه قُسوس أيضًا، وكذلك القِسِّيس، مثل الشَّر والشِّرِّير. ويُقال في جمع قِسِّيس تكسيرًا: قَساوِسَة، بإبدال إحدى السينين واوًا، والأصل قَسّاسَة. فالمراد بالقسيسين في الآية: المتّبعون للعلماء والعُبّاد، وهو إما عَجَمي خلطته العرب بكلامها، أو عربي. والرُّهبان: جمع راهب كرُكبان وراكب، والفعل رَهِبَ اللهَ يَرْهَبُه، أي خافه. والرهبانية والتَّرَهُّب: التعبد في الصوامع. قال أبو عبيد: وقد يكون رُهبان للواحد والجمع.

قال الفراء: ويُجمع رُهبان إذا كان للمفرد رُهبان: رَهابِين، كقُربان وقَرابين. وقد قال جرير في الجمع:

رُهْبانُ مَدْيَنَ لَوْ رَأوْكَ تَرَهَّبُوا

وقال الشاعر في استعمال رُهبان مفردًا:

لَوْ أبْصَرَتْ رُهْبانَ دَيْرٍ في الجَبَلِ ∗∗∗ لانْحَدَرَ الرُّهْبانُ يَسْعى ونَزَلَ

ثم وصفهم الله سبحانه بأنهم لا يستكبرون عن قول الحق، بل هم متواضعون، بخلاف اليهود فإنهم على ضد ذلك. وهذه الجملة معطوفة على الجملة التي قبلها ﴿وإذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إلى الرَّسُولِ﴾ معطوف على جملة ﴿وأنَّهم لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾.

﴿تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ﴾ أي: تمتلئ فتفيض؛ لأن الفيض لا يكون إلا بعد الامتلاء، جعل الأعين تفيض، والفائض إنما هو الدمع، قصدًا للمبالغة كقولهم: دمعت عينه. قال امرؤ القيس:

فَفاضَتْ دُمُوعُ العَيْنِ مِنِّي صَبابَةً ∗∗∗ عَلى النَّحْرِ حَتّى بَلَّ دَمْعِيَ مِحْمَلِي

قوله: ﴿مِمّا عَرَفُوا مِنَ الحَقِّ﴾: "مِن" الأولى لابتداء الغاية، والثانية بيانية، أي: كان ابتداء الفيض ناشئًا من معرفة الحق. ويجوز أن تكون الثانية تبعيضية. وقُرئ ﴿تُرى أعْيُنُهم﴾ على البناء للمجهول.

وقوله: ﴿يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا آمَنّا﴾ استئناف مَسوق لجواب سؤال مقدّر، كأنه قيل: فما حالهم عند سماع القرآن؟ فقال: ﴿يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا آمَنّا فاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾، أي: آمنّا بهذا الكتاب النازل من عندك على محمد وبمن أنزلته عليه، فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين على الناس يوم القيامة من أمة محمد، أو مع الشاهدين بأنه حق، أو مع الشاهدين بصدق محمد وأنه رسولك إلى الناس. قوله: ﴿وما لَنا لا نُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ﴾ كلام مستأنف، والاستفهام للاستبعاد، و"لنا" متعلق بمحذوف، و"لا نؤمن" في محل نصب على الحال، والتقدير: أي شيء حصل لنا حال كوننا لا نؤمن بالله وبما جاءنا من الحق؟ والمعنى: أنهم استبعدوا انتفاء الإيمان منهم مع وجود المقتضي له، وهو الطمع في إنعام الله، فالاستفهام والنفي متوجهان إلى القيد والمقيَّد جميعًا، كقوله تعالى: ﴿ما لَكم لا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وقارًا﴾ [نوح: ١٣]. والواو في ﴿ونَطْمَعُ أنْ يُدْخِلَنا رَبُّنا مَعَ القَوْمِ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ للحال أيضًا بتقدير مبتدأ، أي: أي شيء حصل لنا غير مؤمنين ونحن نطمع في الدخول مع الصالحين؟ فالحال الأولى والثانية صاحبهما الضمير في "لنا" وعاملهما الفعل المقدّر، أي: حصل، ويجوز أن تكون الحال الثانية من الضمير في "نؤمن"، والتقدير: وما لنا نجمع بين ترك الإيمان وبين الطمع في صحبة الصالحين. قوله: ﴿فَأثابَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِما قالُوا﴾ إلخ: أثابهم على هذا القول مخلصين له معتقدين لمضمونه. قوله: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا أُولَئِكَ أصْحابُ الجَحِيمِ﴾: التكذيب بالآيات كفر، فهو من باب عطف الخاص على العام. والجحيم: النار الشديدة الإيقاد، ويُقال: جَحَم فلانٌ النارَ إذا شدّد إيقادها، ويُقال أيضًا لعين الأسد: جُحْمة لشدة اتقادها. قال الشاعر:

والحَرْبُ لا تُبْقِي لِجاحِمِها التَّحَيُّلَ والمِزاحَ

وقد أخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ عن مجاهد في قوله: ﴿ولَتَجِدَنَّ أقْرَبَهم مَوَدَّةً﴾ الآية، قال: هم الوفد الذين جاءوا مع جعفر وأصحابه من أرض الحبشة. وأخرج أبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله (ﷺ): «ما خلا يهوديٌّ بمسلمٍ إلا هَمَّ بقتله»، وفي لفظ: «إلا حدّث نفسه بقتله». قال ابن كثير: وهو غريب جدًا. وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عطاء قال: ما ذكر الله به النصارى من خير فإنما يراد به النجاشي وأصحابه. وأخرج أبو الشيخ عنه قال: هم ناس من الحبشة آمنوا إذا جاءتهم مهاجرة المؤمنين فذلك لهم.

وأخرج النسائي وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم والطبراني وأبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن عبد الله بن الزبير قال: نزلت هذه الآية في النجاشي وأصحابه ﴿وإذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إلى الرَّسُولِ تَرى أعْيُنَهم تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ﴾. وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة وابن أبي حاتم وأبو نعيم في الحلية والواحدي من طريق ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني سعيد بن المسيّب وأبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام وعروة بن الزبير قالوا: «بعث رسول الله (ﷺ) عمرو بن أمية الضَّمْري وكتب معه كتابًا إلى النجاشي، فقدم على النجاشي فقرأ كتاب رسول الله (ﷺ)، ثم دعا جعفر بن أبي طالب والمهاجرين معه، وأرسل النجاشي إلى الرهبان والقسيسين فجمعهم، ثم أمر جعفر بن أبي طالب أن يقرأ عليهم القرآن، فقرأ عليهم سورة مريم، فآمنوا بالقرآن وفاضت أعينهم من الدمع، وهم الذين أنزل الله فيهم ﴿ولَتَجِدَنَّ أقْرَبَهم مَوَدَّةً﴾ إلى قوله: ﴿مِنَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾».

وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن سعيد بن جبير في الآية قال: هم رسل النجاشي بإسلامه وإسلام قومه، كانوا سبعين رجلًا يختارهم من قومه الخيِّر فالخيِّر في الفقه والسنن، وفي لفظ: بعث من خيار أصحابه إلى رسول الله (ﷺ) ثلاثين رجلًا، فلما أتوا رسول الله (ﷺ) دخلوا عليه فقرأ عليهم سورة يس، فبكوا حين سمعوا القرآن وعرفوا أنه الحق، فأنزل الله فيهم: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّ مِنهم قِسِّيسِينَ ورُهْبانًا﴾ الآية، ونزلت هذه الآية فيهم أيضًا: ﴿الَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الكِتابَ مِن قَبْلِهِ هم بِهِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ [القصص: ٥٢] إلى قوله: [p-390] ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أجْرَهم مَرَّتَيْنِ بِما صَبَرُوا﴾ [القصص: ٥٤]. وأخرج عبد بن حميد والطبراني وأبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس نحوه بدون ذكر العدد.

وأخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن السُّدّي قال: بعث النجاشي إلى رسول الله (ﷺ) اثني عشر رجلًا: سبعةً قسِّيسين وخمسةً رهبانًا، ينظرون إليه ويسألونه، فلما لقوه فقرأ عليهم ما أنزل الله بكوا وآمنوا، فأنزل الله فيهم: ﴿وإذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إلى الرَّسُولِ﴾ الآية. والروايات في هذا الباب كثيرة، وهذا المقدار يكفي، فليس المراد إلا بيان سبب نزول الآية. وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحسن في قوله: ﴿قِسِّيسِينَ﴾ قال: هم علماؤهم. وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن زيد قال: القسيسون عبّادهم. وأخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم والحاكم وصححه وابن مردويه من طرق عن ابن عباس في قوله: ﴿فاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾ قال: أمة محمد (ﷺ).

يُصْبِحْنَ عَنْ قَسِّ الأذى غَوافِلا وتَقَسَّسَتْ أصْواتُهم بِاللَّيْلِ تَسْمِعْتُها

والقَسُّ: النميمة. والقَسُّ أيضًا: رئيس النصارى في الدين والعلم، وجمعه قُسوس أيضًا، وكذلك القِسِّيس، مثل الشَّر والشِّرِّير. ويُقال في جمع قِسِّيس تكسيرًا: قَساوِسَة، بإبدال إحدى السينين واوًا، والأصل قَسّاسَة. فالمراد بالقسيسين في الآية: المتّبعون للعلماء والعُبّاد، وهو إما عَجَمي خلطته العرب بكلامها، أو عربي. والرُّهبان: جمع راهب كرُكبان وراكب، والفعل رَهِبَ اللهَ يَرْهَبُه، أي خافه. والرهبانية والتَّرَهُّب: التعبد في الصوامع. قال أبو عبيد: وقد يكون رُهبان للواحد والجمع.

قال الفراء: ويُجمع رُهبان إذا كان للمفرد رُهبان: رَهابِين، كقُربان وقَرابين. وقد قال جرير في الجمع:

رُهْبانُ مَدْيَنَ لَوْ رَأوْكَ تَرَهَّبُوا

وقال الشاعر في استعمال رُهبان مفردًا:

لَوْ أبْصَرَتْ رُهْبانَ دَيْرٍ في الجَبَلِ ∗∗∗ لانْحَدَرَ الرُّهْبانُ يَسْعى ونَزَلَ

ثم وصفهم الله سبحانه بأنهم لا يستكبرون عن قول الحق، بل هم متواضعون، بخلاف اليهود فإنهم على ضد ذلك. وهذه الجملة معطوفة على الجملة التي قبلها ﴿وإذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إلى الرَّسُولِ﴾ معطوف على جملة ﴿وأنَّهم لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾.

﴿تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ﴾ أي: تمتلئ فتفيض؛ لأن الفيض لا يكون إلا بعد الامتلاء، جعل الأعين تفيض، والفائض إنما هو الدمع، قصدًا للمبالغة كقولهم: دمعت عينه. قال امرؤ القيس:

فَفاضَتْ دُمُوعُ العَيْنِ مِنِّي صَبابَةً ∗∗∗ عَلى النَّحْرِ حَتّى بَلَّ دَمْعِيَ مِحْمَلِي

قوله: ﴿مِمّا عَرَفُوا مِنَ الحَقِّ﴾: "مِن" الأولى لابتداء الغاية، والثانية بيانية، أي: كان ابتداء الفيض ناشئًا من معرفة الحق. ويجوز أن تكون الثانية تبعيضية. وقُرئ ﴿تُرى أعْيُنُهم﴾ على البناء للمجهول.

وقوله: ﴿يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا آمَنّا﴾ استئناف مَسوق لجواب سؤال مقدّر، كأنه قيل: فما حالهم عند سماع القرآن؟ فقال: ﴿يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا آمَنّا فاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾، أي: آمنّا بهذا الكتاب النازل من عندك على محمد وبمن أنزلته عليه، فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين على الناس يوم القيامة من أمة محمد، أو مع الشاهدين بأنه حق، أو مع الشاهدين بصدق محمد وأنه رسولك إلى الناس. قوله: ﴿وما لَنا لا نُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ﴾ كلام مستأنف، والاستفهام للاستبعاد، و"لنا" متعلق بمحذوف، و"لا نؤمن" في محل نصب على الحال، والتقدير: أي شيء حصل لنا حال كوننا لا نؤمن بالله وبما جاءنا من الحق؟ والمعنى: أنهم استبعدوا انتفاء الإيمان منهم مع وجود المقتضي له، وهو الطمع في إنعام الله، فالاستفهام والنفي متوجهان إلى القيد والمقيَّد جميعًا، كقوله تعالى: ﴿ما لَكم لا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وقارًا﴾ [نوح: ١٣]. والواو في ﴿ونَطْمَعُ أنْ يُدْخِلَنا رَبُّنا مَعَ القَوْمِ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ للحال أيضًا بتقدير مبتدأ، أي: أي شيء حصل لنا غير مؤمنين ونحن نطمع في الدخول مع الصالحين؟ فالحال الأولى والثانية صاحبهما الضمير في "لنا" وعاملهما الفعل المقدّر، أي: حصل، ويجوز أن تكون الحال الثانية من الضمير في "نؤمن"، والتقدير: وما لنا نجمع بين ترك الإيمان وبين الطمع في صحبة الصالحين. قوله: ﴿فَأثابَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِما قالُوا﴾ إلخ: أثابهم على هذا القول مخلصين له معتقدين لمضمونه. قوله: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا أُولَئِكَ أصْحابُ الجَحِيمِ﴾: التكذيب بالآيات كفر، فهو من باب عطف الخاص على العام. والجحيم: النار الشديدة الإيقاد، ويُقال: جَحَم فلانٌ النارَ إذا شدّد إيقادها، ويُقال أيضًا لعين الأسد: جُحْمة لشدة اتقادها. قال الشاعر:

والحَرْبُ لا تُبْقِي لِجاحِمِها التَّحَيُّلَ والمِزاحَ

والقَسُّ: النميمة. والقَسُّ أيضًا: رئيس النصارى في الدين والعلم، وجمعه قُسوس أيضًا، وكذلك القِسِّيس، مثل الشَّر والشِّرِّير. ويُقال في جمع قِسِّيس تكسيرًا: قَساوِسَة، بإبدال إحدى السينين واوًا، والأصل قَسّاسَة. فالمراد بالقسيسين في الآية: المتّبعون للعلماء والعُبّاد، وهو إما عَجَمي خلطته العرب بكلامها، أو عربي. والرُّهبان: جمع راهب كرُكبان وراكب، والفعل رَهِبَ اللهَ يَرْهَبُه، أي خافه. والرهبانية والتَّرَهُّب: التعبد في الصوامع. قال أبو عبيد: وقد يكون رُهبان للواحد والجمع.

قال الفراء: ويُجمع رُهبان إذا كان للمفرد رُهبان: رَهابِين، كقُربان وقَرابين. وقد قال جرير في الجمع:

رُهْبانُ مَدْيَنَ لَوْ رَأوْكَ تَرَهَّبُوا

وقال الشاعر في استعمال رُهبان مفردًا:

لَوْ أبْصَرَتْ رُهْبانَ دَيْرٍ في الجَبَلِ ∗∗∗ لانْحَدَرَ الرُّهْبانُ يَسْعى ونَزَلَ

ثم وصفهم الله سبحانه بأنهم لا يستكبرون عن قول الحق، بل هم متواضعون، بخلاف اليهود فإنهم على ضد ذلك. وهذه الجملة معطوفة على الجملة التي قبلها ﴿وإذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إلى الرَّسُولِ﴾ معطوف على جملة ﴿وأنَّهم لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾.

﴿تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ﴾ أي: تمتلئ فتفيض؛ لأن الفيض لا يكون إلا بعد الامتلاء، جعل الأعين تفيض، والفائض إنما هو الدمع، قصدًا للمبالغة كقولهم: دمعت عينه. قال امرؤ القيس:

فَفاضَتْ دُمُوعُ العَيْنِ مِنِّي صَبابَةً ∗∗∗ عَلى النَّحْرِ حَتّى بَلَّ دَمْعِيَ مِحْمَلِي

قوله: ﴿مِمّا عَرَفُوا مِنَ الحَقِّ﴾: "مِن" الأولى لابتداء الغاية، والثانية بيانية، أي: كان ابتداء الفيض ناشئًا من معرفة الحق. ويجوز أن تكون الثانية تبعيضية. وقُرئ ﴿تُرى أعْيُنُهم﴾ على البناء للمجهول.

وقوله: ﴿يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا آمَنّا﴾ استئناف مَسوق لجواب سؤال مقدّر، كأنه قيل: فما حالهم عند سماع القرآن؟ فقال: ﴿يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا آمَنّا فاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾، أي: آمنّا بهذا الكتاب النازل من عندك على محمد وبمن أنزلته عليه، فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين على الناس يوم القيامة من أمة محمد، أو مع الشاهدين بأنه حق، أو مع الشاهدين بصدق محمد وأنه رسولك إلى الناس. قوله: ﴿وما لَنا لا نُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ﴾ كلام مستأنف، والاستفهام للاستبعاد، و"لنا" متعلق بمحذوف، و"لا نؤمن" في محل نصب على الحال، والتقدير: أي شيء حصل لنا حال كوننا لا نؤمن بالله وبما جاءنا من الحق؟ والمعنى: أنهم استبعدوا انتفاء الإيمان منهم مع وجود المقتضي له، وهو الطمع في إنعام الله، فالاستفهام والنفي متوجهان إلى القيد والمقيَّد جميعًا، كقوله تعالى: ﴿ما لَكم لا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وقارًا﴾ [نوح: ١٣]. والواو في ﴿ونَطْمَعُ أنْ يُدْخِلَنا رَبُّنا مَعَ القَوْمِ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ للحال أيضًا بتقدير مبتدأ، أي: أي شيء حصل لنا غير مؤمنين ونحن نطمع في الدخول مع الصالحين؟ فالحال الأولى والثانية صاحبهما الضمير في "لنا" وعاملهما الفعل المقدّر، أي: حصل، ويجوز أن تكون الحال الثانية من الضمير في "نؤمن"، والتقدير: وما لنا نجمع بين ترك الإيمان وبين الطمع في صحبة الصالحين. قوله: ﴿فَأثابَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِما قالُوا﴾ إلخ: أثابهم على هذا القول مخلصين له معتقدين لمضمونه. قوله: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا أُولَئِكَ أصْحابُ الجَحِيمِ﴾: التكذيب بالآيات كفر، فهو من باب عطف الخاص على العام. والجحيم: النار الشديدة الإيقاد، ويُقال: جَحَم فلانٌ النارَ إذا شدّد إيقادها، ويُقال أيضًا لعين الأسد: جُحْمة لشدة اتقادها. قال الشاعر:

والحَرْبُ لا تُبْقِي لِجاحِمِها التَّحَيُّلَ والمِزاحَ

وقد أخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ عن مجاهد في قوله: ﴿ولَتَجِدَنَّ أقْرَبَهم مَوَدَّةً﴾ الآية، قال: هم الوفد الذين جاءوا مع جعفر وأصحابه من أرض الحبشة. وأخرج أبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله (ﷺ): «ما خلا يهوديٌّ بمسلمٍ إلا هَمَّ بقتله»، وفي لفظ: «إلا حدّث نفسه بقتله». قال ابن كثير: وهو غريب جدًا. وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عطاء قال: ما ذكر الله به النصارى من خير فإنما يراد به النجاشي وأصحابه. وأخرج أبو الشيخ عنه قال: هم ناس من الحبشة آمنوا إذا جاءتهم مهاجرة المؤمنين فذلك لهم.

وأخرج النسائي وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم والطبراني وأبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن عبد الله بن الزبير قال: نزلت هذه الآية في النجاشي وأصحابه ﴿وإذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إلى الرَّسُولِ تَرى أعْيُنَهم تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ﴾. وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة وابن أبي حاتم وأبو نعيم في الحلية والواحدي من طريق ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني سعيد بن المسيّب وأبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام وعروة بن الزبير قالوا: «بعث رسول الله (ﷺ) عمرو بن أمية الضَّمْري وكتب معه كتابًا إلى النجاشي، فقدم على النجاشي فقرأ كتاب رسول الله (ﷺ)، ثم دعا جعفر بن أبي طالب والمهاجرين معه، وأرسل النجاشي إلى الرهبان والقسيسين فجمعهم، ثم أمر جعفر بن أبي طالب أن يقرأ عليهم القرآن، فقرأ عليهم سورة مريم، فآمنوا بالقرآن وفاضت أعينهم من الدمع، وهم الذين أنزل الله فيهم ﴿ولَتَجِدَنَّ أقْرَبَهم مَوَدَّةً﴾ إلى قوله: ﴿مِنَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾».

وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن سعيد بن جبير في الآية قال: هم رسل النجاشي بإسلامه وإسلام قومه، كانوا سبعين رجلًا يختارهم من قومه الخيِّر فالخيِّر في الفقه والسنن، وفي لفظ: بعث من خيار أصحابه إلى رسول الله (ﷺ) ثلاثين رجلًا، فلما أتوا رسول الله (ﷺ) دخلوا عليه فقرأ عليهم سورة يس، فبكوا حين سمعوا القرآن وعرفوا أنه الحق، فأنزل الله فيهم: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّ مِنهم قِسِّيسِينَ ورُهْبانًا﴾ الآية، ونزلت هذه الآية فيهم أيضًا: ﴿الَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الكِتابَ مِن قَبْلِهِ هم بِهِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ [القصص: ٥٢] إلى قوله: [p-390] ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أجْرَهم مَرَّتَيْنِ بِما صَبَرُوا﴾ [القصص: ٥٤]. وأخرج عبد بن حميد والطبراني وأبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس نحوه بدون ذكر العدد.

وأخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن السُّدّي قال: بعث النجاشي إلى رسول الله (ﷺ) اثني عشر رجلًا: سبعةً قسِّيسين وخمسةً رهبانًا، ينظرون إليه ويسألونه، فلما لقوه فقرأ عليهم ما أنزل الله بكوا وآمنوا، فأنزل الله فيهم: ﴿وإذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إلى الرَّسُولِ﴾ الآية. والروايات في هذا الباب كثيرة، وهذا المقدار يكفي، فليس المراد إلا بيان سبب نزول الآية. وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحسن في قوله: ﴿قِسِّيسِينَ﴾ قال: هم علماؤهم. وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن زيد قال: القسيسون عبّادهم. وأخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم والحاكم وصححه وابن مردويه من طرق عن ابن عباس في قوله: ﴿فاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾ قال: أمة محمد (ﷺ).
