وقوله: ﴿يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا آمَنّا﴾ استئناف مَسوق لجواب سؤال مقدّر، كأنه قيل: فما حالهم عند سماع القرآن؟ فقال: ﴿يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا آمَنّا فاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾، أي: آمنّا بهذا الكتاب النازل من عندك على محمد وبمن أنزلته عليه، فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين على الناس يوم القيامة من أمة محمد، أو مع الشاهدين بأنه حق، أو مع الشاهدين بصدق محمد وأنه رسولك إلى الناس. قوله: ﴿وما لَنا لا نُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ﴾ كلام مستأنف، والاستفهام للاستبعاد، و"لنا" متعلق بمحذوف، و"لا نؤمن" في محل نصب على الحال، والتقدير: أي شيء حصل لنا حال كوننا لا نؤمن بالله وبما جاءنا من الحق؟ والمعنى: أنهم استبعدوا انتفاء الإيمان منهم مع وجود المقتضي له، وهو الطمع في إنعام الله، فالاستفهام والنفي متوجهان إلى القيد والمقيَّد جميعًا، كقوله تعالى: ﴿ما لَكم لا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وقارًا﴾ [نوح: ١٣]. والواو في ﴿ونَطْمَعُ أنْ يُدْخِلَنا رَبُّنا مَعَ القَوْمِ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ للحال أيضًا بتقدير مبتدأ، أي: أي شيء حصل لنا غير مؤمنين ونحن نطمع في الدخول مع الصالحين؟ فالحال الأولى والثانية صاحبهما الضمير في "لنا" وعاملهما الفعل المقدّر، أي: حصل، ويجوز أن تكون الحال الثانية من الضمير في "نؤمن"، والتقدير: وما لنا نجمع بين ترك الإيمان وبين الطمع في صحبة الصالحين. قوله: ﴿فَأثابَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِما قالُوا﴾ إلخ: أثابهم على هذا القول مخلصين له معتقدين لمضمونه. قوله: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا أُولَئِكَ أصْحابُ الجَحِيمِ﴾: التكذيب بالآيات كفر، فهو من باب عطف الخاص على العام. والجحيم: النار الشديدة الإيقاد، ويُقال: جَحَم فلانٌ النارَ إذا شدّد إيقادها، ويُقال أيضًا لعين الأسد: جُحْمة لشدة اتقادها. قال الشاعر:

والحَرْبُ لا تُبْقِي لِجاحِمِها التَّحَيُّلَ والمِزاحَ

وقد أخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ عن مجاهد في قوله: ﴿ولَتَجِدَنَّ أقْرَبَهم مَوَدَّةً﴾ الآية، قال: هم الوفد الذين جاءوا مع جعفر وأصحابه من أرض الحبشة. وأخرج أبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله (ﷺ): «ما خلا يهوديٌّ بمسلمٍ إلا هَمَّ بقتله»، وفي لفظ: «إلا حدّث نفسه بقتله». قال ابن كثير: وهو غريب جدًا. وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عطاء قال: ما ذكر الله به النصارى من خير فإنما يراد به النجاشي وأصحابه. وأخرج أبو الشيخ عنه قال: هم ناس من الحبشة آمنوا إذا جاءتهم مهاجرة المؤمنين فذلك لهم.

وأخرج النسائي وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم والطبراني وأبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن عبد الله بن الزبير قال: نزلت هذه الآية في النجاشي وأصحابه ﴿وإذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إلى الرَّسُولِ تَرى أعْيُنَهم تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ﴾. وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة وابن أبي حاتم وأبو نعيم في الحلية والواحدي من طريق ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني سعيد بن المسيّب وأبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام وعروة بن الزبير قالوا: «بعث رسول الله (ﷺ) عمرو بن أمية الضَّمْري وكتب معه كتابًا إلى النجاشي، فقدم على النجاشي فقرأ كتاب رسول الله (ﷺ)، ثم دعا جعفر بن أبي طالب والمهاجرين معه، وأرسل النجاشي إلى الرهبان والقسيسين فجمعهم، ثم أمر جعفر بن أبي طالب أن يقرأ عليهم القرآن، فقرأ عليهم سورة مريم، فآمنوا بالقرآن وفاضت أعينهم من الدمع، وهم الذين أنزل الله فيهم ﴿ولَتَجِدَنَّ أقْرَبَهم مَوَدَّةً﴾ إلى قوله: ﴿مِنَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾».

وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن سعيد بن جبير في الآية قال: هم رسل النجاشي بإسلامه وإسلام قومه، كانوا سبعين رجلًا يختارهم من قومه الخيِّر فالخيِّر في الفقه والسنن، وفي لفظ: بعث من خيار أصحابه إلى رسول الله (ﷺ) ثلاثين رجلًا، فلما أتوا رسول الله (ﷺ) دخلوا عليه فقرأ عليهم سورة يس، فبكوا حين سمعوا القرآن وعرفوا أنه الحق، فأنزل الله فيهم: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّ مِنهم قِسِّيسِينَ ورُهْبانًا﴾ الآية، ونزلت هذه الآية فيهم أيضًا: ﴿الَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الكِتابَ مِن قَبْلِهِ هم بِهِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ [القصص: ٥٢] إلى قوله: [p-390] ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أجْرَهم مَرَّتَيْنِ بِما صَبَرُوا﴾ [القصص: ٥٤]. وأخرج عبد بن حميد والطبراني وأبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس نحوه بدون ذكر العدد.

وأخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن السُّدّي قال: بعث النجاشي إلى رسول الله (ﷺ) اثني عشر رجلًا: سبعةً قسِّيسين وخمسةً رهبانًا، ينظرون إليه ويسألونه، فلما لقوه فقرأ عليهم ما أنزل الله بكوا وآمنوا، فأنزل الله فيهم: ﴿وإذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إلى الرَّسُولِ﴾ الآية. والروايات في هذا الباب كثيرة، وهذا المقدار يكفي، فليس المراد إلا بيان سبب نزول الآية. وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحسن في قوله: ﴿قِسِّيسِينَ﴾ قال: هم علماؤهم. وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن زيد قال: القسيسون عبّادهم. وأخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم والحاكم وصححه وابن مردويه من طرق عن ابن عباس في قوله: ﴿فاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾ قال: أمة محمد (ﷺ).

﴿لَتَجِدَنَّ﴾ إلخ: هذه جملة مستأنفة تقرر ما فيها من تعداد مساوئ اليهود وعيوبهم، ودخول لام القسم عليها يزيدها تأكيدًا وتقريرًا. والخطاب لرسول الله (ﷺ)، أو لكل من يصلح له، كما في غير هذا الموضع من الكتاب العزيز. والمعنى في الآية: أن اليهود والمشركين، لعنهم الله، أشد جميع الناس عداوةً للمؤمنين وأصلبهم في ذلك، وأن النصارى أقرب الناس مودةً للمؤمنين. واللام في ﴿لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ في الموضعين متعلقة بمحذوف وقع صفةً لعداوةٍ ومودةٍ، وقيل هي متعلقة بعداوةٍ ومودةٍ. والإشارة بقوله: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ إلى كونهم أقرب مودةً. والباء في ﴿بِأنَّ مِنهم قِسِّيسِينَ﴾ للسببية، أي: ذلك بسبب أن منهم قسيسين، وهو جمع قِسٍّ وقِسِّيسٍ، قاله قُطرب. والقِسِّيس: العالم، وأصله من قَسَّ إذا تتبّع الشيء وطلبه. قال الراجز:

يُصْبِحْنَ عَنْ قَسِّ الأذى غَوافِلا وتَقَسَّسَتْ أصْواتُهم بِاللَّيْلِ تَسْمِعْتُها

والقَسُّ: النميمة. والقَسُّ أيضًا: رئيس النصارى في الدين والعلم، وجمعه قُسوس أيضًا، وكذلك القِسِّيس، مثل الشَّر والشِّرِّير. ويُقال في جمع قِسِّيس تكسيرًا: قَساوِسَة، بإبدال إحدى السينين واوًا، والأصل قَسّاسَة. فالمراد بالقسيسين في الآية: المتّبعون للعلماء والعُبّاد، وهو إما عَجَمي خلطته العرب بكلامها، أو عربي. والرُّهبان: جمع راهب كرُكبان وراكب، والفعل رَهِبَ اللهَ يَرْهَبُه، أي خافه. والرهبانية والتَّرَهُّب: التعبد في الصوامع. قال أبو عبيد: وقد يكون رُهبان للواحد والجمع.

قال الفراء: ويُجمع رُهبان إذا كان للمفرد رُهبان: رَهابِين، كقُربان وقَرابين. وقد قال جرير في الجمع:

رُهْبانُ مَدْيَنَ لَوْ رَأوْكَ تَرَهَّبُوا

وقال الشاعر في استعمال رُهبان مفردًا:

لَوْ أبْصَرَتْ رُهْبانَ دَيْرٍ في الجَبَلِ ∗∗∗ لانْحَدَرَ الرُّهْبانُ يَسْعى ونَزَلَ

ثم وصفهم الله سبحانه بأنهم لا يستكبرون عن قول الحق، بل هم متواضعون، بخلاف اليهود فإنهم على ضد ذلك. وهذه الجملة معطوفة على الجملة التي قبلها ﴿وإذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إلى الرَّسُولِ﴾ معطوف على جملة ﴿وأنَّهم لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾.

﴿تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ﴾ أي: تمتلئ فتفيض؛ لأن الفيض لا يكون إلا بعد الامتلاء، جعل الأعين تفيض، والفائض إنما هو الدمع، قصدًا للمبالغة كقولهم: دمعت عينه. قال امرؤ القيس:

فَفاضَتْ دُمُوعُ العَيْنِ مِنِّي صَبابَةً ∗∗∗ عَلى النَّحْرِ حَتّى بَلَّ دَمْعِيَ مِحْمَلِي

وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن سعيد بن جبير في الآية قال: هم رسل النجاشي بإسلامه وإسلام قومه، كانوا سبعين رجلًا يختارهم من قومه الخيِّر فالخيِّر في الفقه والسنن، وفي لفظ: بعث من خيار أصحابه إلى رسول الله (ﷺ) ثلاثين رجلًا، فلما أتوا رسول الله (ﷺ) دخلوا عليه فقرأ عليهم سورة يس، فبكوا حين سمعوا القرآن وعرفوا أنه الحق، فأنزل الله فيهم: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّ مِنهم قِسِّيسِينَ ورُهْبانًا﴾ الآية، ونزلت هذه الآية فيهم أيضًا: ﴿الَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الكِتابَ مِن قَبْلِهِ هم بِهِ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ [القصص: ٥٢] إلى قوله: [p-390] ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أجْرَهم مَرَّتَيْنِ بِما صَبَرُوا﴾ [القصص: ٥٤]. وأخرج عبد بن حميد والطبراني وأبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس نحوه بدون ذكر العدد.

وأخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن السُّدّي قال: بعث النجاشي إلى رسول الله (ﷺ) اثني عشر رجلًا: سبعةً قسِّيسين وخمسةً رهبانًا، ينظرون إليه ويسألونه، فلما لقوه فقرأ عليهم ما أنزل الله بكوا وآمنوا، فأنزل الله فيهم: ﴿وإذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إلى الرَّسُولِ﴾ الآية. والروايات في هذا الباب كثيرة، وهذا المقدار يكفي، فليس المراد إلا بيان سبب نزول الآية. وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحسن في قوله: ﴿قِسِّيسِينَ﴾ قال: هم علماؤهم. وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن زيد قال: القسيسون عبّادهم. وأخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم والحاكم وصححه وابن مردويه من طرق عن ابن عباس في قوله: ﴿فاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾ قال: أمة محمد (ﷺ).

al-Tayyibat: those things that are pleasant and delightful of what Allah has made lawful for His servants. He forbade those who believe from forbidding upon themselves any of them, either because they think that doing so is obedience to Allah and a means of drawing near to Him, and that it is part of renunciation of the world to lift the self above its desires; or with the intention of forbidding to themselves something that He has made lawful for them, as occurs among many of the common people in their saying: "It is haram upon me," "I have made it haram for myself," and similar expressions that fall under this Qur'anic prohibition.

Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: It is not permissible for any of the Muslims to forbid upon himself anything of what Allah has made lawful for His believing servants, of the good foods, clothing and marriages. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) rejected celibacy (al-tabattul) proposed by Uthman ibn Maz'un.

It is therefore established that there is no merit in abandoning anything that Allah has made lawful for His servants, and that merit and righteousness lie only in doing what Allah has urged His servants to do, what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) acted upon and established as a sunnah for his community, and what the rightly-guided Imams followed in his way, since the best guidance is the guidance of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Given that this is so, it becomes clear that the error of one who prefers wearing hair and wool over wearing cotton and linen, when he is able to wear the latter lawfully, and who prefers eating coarse food and leaving meat and other things, out of fear of the incidental need for women, is evident.

He said: If someone supposes that the merit lies in something other than what we have stated, because of the hardship upon the self in wearing coarse clothing and eating coarse food, and in diverting the surplus value between them to people in need, then he has erred in his supposition. That is because the first priority for a person is the well-being of his self and aiding it to obey its Lord; and nothing harms the body more than bad foods, since they corrupt his intellect and weaken the faculties that Allah has made a means to His obedience.

His saying: ﴿And do not transgress﴾ means: do not transgress against Allah by forbidding the good things that Allah has made lawful for you; or do not transgress by making lawful what Allah has forbidden to you; that is, do not be lax so as to make lawful what is unlawful, just as you were forbidden to be strict upon yourselves by forbidding what is lawful. The majority of scholars have held that whoever forbids upon himself something that Allah has made lawful for him, it does not become forbidden for him, and he is not obliged to an expiation (kaffarah).

Abu Hanifah, Ahmad, and those who follow them said: whoever forbids something becomes bound by its prohibition, and if he consumes it he is obliged to expiation. This is contrary to what is in this verse and contrary to what the authentic hadiths indicate; and perhaps there will come in Surat al-Tahrim what is more detailed than this, Allah willing. His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors﴾ is a reason for what precedes it, and its apparent meaning is the prohibition of every transgression; that is, going beyond what Allah has legislated in every matter.

﴿And eat of what Allah has provided for you﴾ while it is lawful and good, that is: not forbidden nor repugnant; or eat what is lawful and good; or eat lawful and good things of what Allah has provided for you. Then Allah, glorified is He, enjoined upon them taqwa, saying: ﴿And fear Allah, in whom you are believers.﴾ Al-Tirmidhi, who graded it as hasan, and Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Adi in al-Kamil, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, when I eat meat I become aroused toward women and desire seizes me, and I have made meat forbidden to myself." So there was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you.﴾ It has also been narrated by another route as mursal, and narrated as mawquf upon Ibn Abbas.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him concerning the verse, he said: "It was revealed concerning a group of the Companions who said: 'We shall cut off our genitals, abandon the desires of the world, and wander in the earth as the monks do.' This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he sent for them and mentioned that to them. They said: 'Yes.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'But I fast and break my fast, I pray and I sleep, and I marry women. Whoever takes my sunnah is of me, and whoever does not take my sunnah is not of me.'" Something similar has been established in the two Sahihs and others without mention that this was the occasion of revelation of the verse.

Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in al-Marasil, and Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Malik that these group were: Uthman ibn Maz'un and his companions. On this theme there are many narrations, and many of them explicitly state that this was the occasion of revelation of the verse. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam that "Abd Allah ibn Rawahah hosted a guest from his family while he was with the Prophet (ﷺ), then he returned to his family and found that they had not fed their guest, waiting for him. He said to his wife: 'You have detained my guest on my account; it is haram upon me.' His wife said: 'It is haram upon me.' The guest said: 'It is haram upon me.' When he saw that, he put his hand down and said: 'Eat, in the name of Allah.' Then he went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'You have done right.' So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you.'" This is a disconnected report (athar munqati'), but in the Sahih of al-Bukhari there is something similar in the story of al-Siddiq with his guests.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Masruq, who said: "We were with Abd Allah (ibn Mas'ud), and a udder was brought in, and a man drew back. Abd Allah said to him: 'Come near.' He said: 'I have made it forbidden for myself to eat it.' Abd Allah said: 'Come near, eat, and make expiation for your oath,' and he recited this verse." Al-Hakim also narrated it in his Mustadrak and said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it."

The explanation of *laghw* (idle or unintended oaths) and the scholarly disagreement about it has already been given in Surah al-Baqarah. The phrase ﴿fi aymanikum﴾ ("in your oaths") is connected to ﴿yu'akhidhukum﴾ ("He will hold you accountable"). It was said that *fi* here has the sense of *min* ("from"), and *al-aymaan* is the plural of *yameen* (oath).

The verse indicates that Allah does not hold a person accountable for idle oaths and that no expiation (*kaffarah*) is required for them. The majority of the Companions and those after them held that the idle oath is a man's saying, "No, by Allah," or "Yes, by Allah," in his speech without intending an oath. The Companions, who knew the meanings of the Qur'an best, explained the verse in this way. Al-Shafi'i said: "This happens in heated argument, anger and haste."

As for His saying ﴿but He will hold you accountable for what you have bound with oaths﴾: it is recited with the doubled *qaf* in ﴿'aqqadtum﴾ and with the single *qaf*, and it is also recited as ﴿'aqadtum﴾. *Al-'aqd* (binding) is of two kinds: the physical, such as tying a rope, and the legal, such as a contract of sale, an oath and a covenant. A poet said:

> A people who, when they bind a pact for their neighbour, tie the knot tightly and fasten the strap upon it.

So the binding oath is that which the heart binds, meaning that a person resolves that he will or will not do something in the future. The meaning is: "But He will hold you accountable for your binding oaths, which are firmly secured by intention and purpose, when you break them." As for the *ghamus* oath (the perjurious oath, sworn to deceive), it is an oath of deceit, trickery and falsehood, and the swearer bears its sin. It is not a binding oath, and there is no expiation for it, as the majority held. Al-Shafi'i said it is a binding oath, because it is acquired by the heart, binds by a statement, and is connected with the name of Allah. The sounder view is the first. All the hadiths reporting expiation for oaths refer to the binding oath, and none of them indicates the *ghamus*. Rather, what is reported about the *ghamus* is only a warning and a deterrent, and that it is among the major sins, indeed among the greatest of the major sins. Concerning it was revealed the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price...﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 77], to the end of the verse.

As for His saying ﴿fa-kaffaratuhu﴾ ("then its expiation"): *al-kaffarah* is derived from *takfir*, which means covering. Likewise *kufr* means covering, and *kafir* means one who covers, because the expiation covers the sin and conceals it. The pronoun in *kaffaratihi* refers to *ma* in His saying ﴿for what you have bound﴾.

﴿Feeding ten needy persons from the average of what you feed your families﴾: the "average" here means the middle between extravagance and stinginess, and it does not mean the best, as it does in other places. That is, feed them from the middle level of what you are accustomed to feeding your families. It is not obligatory for you to feed them from the best, nor is it permissible for you to feed them from the worst. The apparent meaning is that feeding ten persons is sufficient, even to the point of their being satisfied. It has been narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib that he said: "Feeding the ten is not sufficient with lunch alone without supper, until you feed them lunch and supper." Abu 'Umar said: "This is the view of the leading jurists in the cities." Al-Hasan al-Basri and Ibn Sirin said: "It is sufficient for him to feed ten needy persons one meal, bread with ghee, or bread with meat." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, 'A'ishah, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Maymun ibn Mihran, Abu Malik, al-Dahhak, al-Hakam, Makhul, Abu Qilabah and Muqatil said: "He gives each of the ten half a *sa'* of wheat or dates." This was also narrated from 'Ali. Abu Hanifah said: "Half a *sa'* of wheat, or a *sa'* of other things."

Ibn Majah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made expiation with a *sa'* of dates, and the people made expiation with it. And whoever does not find it, then half a *sa'* of wheat." In its chain is 'Umar ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ya'la al-Thaqafi, who is agreed to be weak. al-Daraqutni said: "Abandoned (matruk)."

As for His saying ﴿or their clothing﴾: it is coordinated with feeding. It is recited with a *damma* and a *kasra* on the *kaf*, and both are dialects, like *uswah* and *iswah*. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa' al-Yamani recited *aw ka-uswatihim*, meaning "like the clothing of your families." Clothing for men is applicable to whatever covers the body, even if it is one garment, and likewise for women's clothing. It was said that clothing for women is a shift (*dir'*) and a head-cover (*khimar*). It was also said that the intended clothing is that with which prayer is valid.

As for His saying ﴿or the freeing of a neck﴾: that is, the manumission of a slave. *Al-tahrir* means removing someone from bondage. The term *tahrir* is also used for freeing a captive, relieving someone exhausted by work from his labour, and avoiding causing harm to him. From this is the saying of al-Farazdaq:

> O Banu Ghudanah, indeed I have freed you, so I have given you as a gift to 'Atiyyah ibn Ji'al.

That is: I have freed you from the satire that would have brought you low and harmed your honour.

The scholars have discussions about the neck that is valid for expiation. The apparent meaning of this verse is that any neck is valid, of whatever description it may be. A group, including al-Shafi'i, held that faith is a condition for it, by analogy with the expiation for killing.

﴿Then whoever does not find [any of these], then fasting three days﴾: that is, whoever does not find any of the matters mentioned, then his expiation is fasting three days. It was recited as *mutatabi'at* ("consecutive"), reported from Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy. This recitation restricts the absolute fasting. This is the view of Abu Hanifah, al-Thawri, and one of the two positions of al-Shafi'i. Malik and al-Shafi'i in his other position said: separation (of the days) is permissible.

﴿That is the expiation of your oaths when you swear﴾: that is, what has been mentioned is the expiation of your oaths when you swear and break them. Then He commanded them to guard their oaths and not to hasten to them or to breaking them. The indication of His saying "thus" (*ka-dhalika*) refers to the verbal noun of the verb mentioned after it. That is: "Like that clarification, Allah makes clear to you." This has been repeated in several places in the Mighty Book. ﴿So that you may be grateful﴾ for what He has bestowed upon you by clarifying His laws and explaining His rulings.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: When this was revealed, ﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things Allah has made lawful for you﴾, concerning the people who had forbidden for themselves women and meat, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, how should we deal with our oaths by which we swore?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for idle oaths in your oaths.﴾

Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning *laghw*, that he said: "It is the man who swears about something lawful."

Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Mujahid that he said: "They are two men who trade with each other. One says: 'By Allah, I will not sell it to you for such-and-such,' and the other says: 'By Allah, I will not buy it for such-and-such.'"

Abd ibn Humayd and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Nakha'i that he said: "*Laghw* is that a person connects his speech with an oath: 'By Allah, you will eat,' 'By Allah, you will drink,' and the like, not intending an oath and not deliberately swearing. This is the idle oath, for which there is no expiation." The discussion of this has already been given in al-Baqarah.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid concerning ﴿but He will hold you accountable for what you have bound with oaths﴾, that he said: "For what you have made obligatory upon yourselves (*ta'abbadtum*)." Abd ibn Humayd and Abu al-Shaykh narrated the like from Qatadah.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Umar: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to assess the expiation of an oath as one *mudd* of wheat." In its chain is al-Nadr ibn Zurarah ibn 'Abd al-Karim al-Dhuhli al-Kufi. Abu Hatim said: "Unknown (majhul)," but Ibn Hibban mentioned him in *al-Thiqat*. The hadith of Ibn 'Abbas and its weakness have already been mentioned.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Asma' bint Abi Bakr that she said: "We used to give in the expiation of oaths with the *mudd* by which we sustain ourselves."

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said: "I swear that I will not give to certain people, then it becomes clear to me, and I give them. So I feed ten needy persons, each needy person a *sa'* of barley, or a *sa'* of dates, or half a *sa'* of wheat."

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib that he said: "In the expiation of an oath is feeding ten needy persons, to each needy person half a *sa'* of wheat."

Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Ibn 'Abbas the like of this.

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated by various routes that he said: "In the expiation of an oath is one *mudd* of wheat for each needy person."

These (narrators) all narrated, except Ibn Abi Hatim, from Zayd ibn Thabit the like of this. They also narrated from Ibn 'Umar the like of this. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Abu Hurayrah the like of this.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib that he said: "You feed them lunch and supper, if you wish, bread with meat, or bread with oil, or bread with ghee, or bread with dates."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿from the average of what you feed your families﴾ that he said: "From your hardship and your ease." Ibn Majah narrated from him that he said: "A man would provide his family with a provision that was generous, and a man would provide his family with a provision that was harsh, so this was revealed: ﴿from the average of what you feed your families﴾." Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated similarly from him.

al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'A'ishah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His saying ﴿or their clothing﴾, that he said: "A cloak (*aba'ah*) for each needy person." Ibn Kathir said: "This is a strange hadith (*gharib*)." Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Hudhayfah that he said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, or their clothing, what is it?' He said: 'A cloak, a cloak.'" Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "A cloak for each needy person, or a wrap (*shamlah*)." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Umar that he said: "Clothing is a garment or a waist-wrap." Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi in his *Sunan* narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Concerning the expiation of an oath, he has the choice among these three, in order, first then first. If he does not find any of them, then fasting three consecutive days." Ibn Mardawayh narrated similarly from him.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 5, verse 90–93 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾ is an address to all the believers. The explanation of al-maysir (gambling) has already been given in Surat al-Baqarah. ﴿And the idols (al-ansab)﴾ are the idols set up for worship. ﴿And the arrows (al-azlam)﴾: their explanation has already been given at the beginning of this surah. Al-rijs (filth, impurity) is applied to excrement and filth. It is a predicate of al-khamr (wine), and the predicate of what is conjoined to it is omitted. His saying: ﴿from the work of Satan﴾ is an attribute of rijs; that is, it is something arising from the work of Satan, due to his making it appealing and adorning it for them. It has also been said: he is the one who first performed these matters himself, and the children of Adam followed him. The pronoun in ﴿so avoid it﴾ refers to rijs, or to what was mentioned.

His saying: ﴿so that you may prosper﴾ is a cause for what precedes it. Al-Kashshaf says: The prohibition of wine and gambling has been emphasized in several ways. Among them: beginning the sentence with innama (only/indeed). Among them: he linked them with the worship of idols, and from this is his saying, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace: "The drinker of wine is like the worshipper of an idol." Among them: he made them rijs, as he said: ﴿So avoid the filth of the idols﴾ [al-Hajj: 30]. Among them: he made them from the work of Satan, and Satan brings nothing but pure evil. Among them: he commanded avoidance. Among them: he made avoidance a part of success, and if avoidance is success, then indulgence is failure and loss. Among them: he mentioned the harm that results from them, which is the occurrence of enmity and hatred between the people of wine and gambling, and what they lead to of barring from the remembrance of Allah and from observing the times of the prayers. End of quote.

In this verse there is evidence for the prohibition of wine, because the command to avoid includes obligation, and the prohibition of barring, and because it is established in the Shariah that approaching rijs is forbidden, let alone making it a drink to be drunk. The scholars among the exegetes and others said: The prohibition of wine came gradually and through many occurrences, because they had become accustomed to drinking it and Satan had made it beloved to their hearts. The first thing revealed about it was ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In both is great sin and some benefit for people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 219]. At that point some of the Muslims left drinking it, while others did not leave it. Then the saying of the Exalted was revealed: ﴿Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ [an-Nisa: 43], and some also left it, saying: We have no need for what preoccupies us from prayer. Some drank it at times other than the times of prayer, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, wine and gambling...﴾, and it became forbidden to them, to the extent that some of them would say: Allah has not prohibited anything more severe than wine. This was because of what they understood of the stringency in what this verse contains of warnings, and what the sound hadiths conveyed of threats for its drinker, and that it is among the major sins.

The Muslims have agreed upon this with an agreement beyond any doubt or suspicion. They also agreed on the prohibition of selling it and benefiting from it as long as it is wine. Just as this verse indicates the prohibition of wine, it also indicates the prohibition of gambling, the idols, and the arrows. This verse has pointed to the worldly harms in wine and gambling by His saying: ﴿Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred among you﴾, and to the religious harms by His saying: ﴿and to bar you from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer﴾.

His saying: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ contains an eloquent restraint conveyed by the interrogative that indicates reproach and rebuke. For this reason, Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, when he heard this, said: "We have desisted." Then Allah, glorified is He, reinforced this prohibition with His saying: ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger and beware﴾, that is, of opposing them; that is, opposing Allah and His Messenger. Although this is a general command, mentioning it in this place conveys the emphasis we have mentioned. Likewise what He conveyed by His saying: ﴿But if you turn away, then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification﴾, that is: if you turn away from compliance, the Messenger has done what is obligatory upon him, namely the notification in which is your guidance and welfare, and you have harmed by opposition only yourselves. In this there is a restraint whose measure cannot be estimated and whose extent cannot be reached.

His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾, that is, from the foods which they desire. Although the use of ta'm (eating) is more common for eating, it may also be used for drinking, and from it is His saying: ﴿And whoever does not taste it, he is not of me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 249]. Allah, glorified is He, permitted them in this verse everything they had eaten, whatever it was, restricted by His saying: ﴿when they fear Allah﴾, that is, they refrain from what is forbidden to them, such as wine and other major sins and all acts of disobedience, and believe in Allah and do righteous deeds of those which Allah has prescribed for them; that is, they persist in doing them.

His saying: ﴿Then they feared Allah﴾ is a conjunction with the first "feared Allah"; that is: they refrained from what was prohibited to them after that, although it had been permissible before, and believed in its prohibition. ﴿Then they feared Allah﴾ refers to what was prohibited to them after the aforementioned prohibition, of what had been permissible before, and they did good, that is, they did good deeds. This is the meaning of the verse. It has been said: the repetition is with regard to three times. It has been said: the repetition is with regard to three levels: the beginning, the middle, and the end. It has been said: the repetition is with regard to what a person guards against: he should leave the forbidden things to avoid punishment, the doubtful things to avoid falling into the unlawful, and some permissible things to preserve the self from baseness. It has been said: it is merely for emphasis, as in His saying: ﴿No! You will come to know. Then no! You will come to know﴾ [at-Takathur: 3–4]. All these views, apart from the occasion of revelation, may be considered; or, considering the occasion of its revelation: when the prohibition of wine was revealed, some of the Companions said: "What about one of us who died while drinking it and eating gambling?" Then this was revealed. It has been said that the meaning is: "fear shirk and believe in Allah and His Messenger, then fear [the major sins] and believe," that is, increase in faith, "then fear [the minor sins] and do good," that is, perform voluntary acts.

Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: The first fear is fearing by receiving Allah's command with acceptance, affirmation, submission to it, and action. The second fear is fearing by steadfastness upon affirmation. The third is fearing by doing good and drawing near through voluntary acts. Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab have reported from Ibn Umar who said: "Three verses were revealed concerning wine. The first thing was ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾ [al-Baqarah: 219], the verse. It was said: wine is forbidden. Then it was said: O Messenger of Allah, let us benefit from it as Allah said. He remained silent toward them. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ [an-Nisa: 43]. It was said: wine is forbidden. They said: O Messenger of Allah, we will not drink it near the prayer. He remained silent toward them. Then it was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed wine...﴾, the verse. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: Wine is forbidden."

Ahmad reported from Abu Hurairah who said: "Wine was prohibited three times," and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Umar. People said: "O Messenger of Allah, some people were killed in the way of Allah and died on their beds, while they used to drink wine and eat gambling, and Allah has made it filth from the work of Satan." So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who have believed﴾, the verse. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "If it had been forbidden to them, they would have left it as you have left it."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Nahhas in his Nasikh, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas who said: "The prohibition of wine was revealed concerning me. A man from the Ansar prepared food and invited people, and they came and ate and drank until they became intoxicated with wine, and that was before wine was prohibited. Then they boasted: the Ansar are better than the Muhajirun, and Quraysh said: Quraysh is better. Then a man struck me on the nose with the jawbone of a camel. I came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and mentioned that to him, and then this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed wine and gambling...﴾, the verse."

Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi reported from Ibn Abbas who said: "The prohibition of wine was revealed concerning two tribes of the Ansar who drank. When the people became intoxicated, some of them played with others. When they became sober, one of them would see the mark on his face, head and beard and say: 'My brother so-and-so did this to me,' and they were brothers with no rancor in their hearts. By Allah, if he had been kind and merciful to me he would not have done this to me; until enmity entered their hearts. So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed wine and gambling...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾. Some of the over-zealous people said: 'It is filth, and so-and-so is in its belly, who was killed at Badr, and so-and-so was killed at Uhud.' So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾, the verse." Many narrations concerning the occasion of revelation have been transmitted, agreeing with what we have mentioned.

Abd ibn Humayd reported from Qatadah who said: "Al-maysir is all gambling." Ibn Mardawayh reported from Wahb ibn Kaysan who said: "I said to Jabir: When was wine prohibited? He said: After Uhud." Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Qatadah who said: "The prohibition of wine was revealed in Surat al-Ma'idah, after the Battle of the Confederates." Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn Abbas who said: "All gambling is from al-maysir, even children's playing with walnuts and knucklebones." Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Ali ibn Abi Talib who said: "Backgammon (al-nard) and chess (al-shatranj) are from al-maysir." Abd ibn Humayd reported from Ali who said: "Chess is the gambling of the non-Arabs."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad that he was asked whether backgammon is from al-maysir. He said: "Everything that diverts from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer is maysir." Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Dhamm al-Malahi, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab reported from him as well that it was said to him: "This backgammon you dislike, so what about chess?" He said: "Everything that diverts from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer is from maysir."

They also reported from Ibn al-Zubayr who said: "O people of Makkah, it has reached me that men play with a game called al-nardashir, and Allah says in His Book: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed wine and gambling...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾. I swear by Allah, I will not be brought anyone who plays with it except that I will punish him in his hair and skin, and I will give his spoils to whoever brings him to me." Ibn Abi al-Dunya reported from Malik ibn Anas who said: "Chess is from backgammon. It has reached us from Ibn Abbas that he was in charge of an orphan's wealth and burned it." Ibn Abi al-Dunya reported from Abu Ja'far that he was asked about chess and said: "That is Magianism, so do not play with it." Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi al-Dunya reported from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "Whoever plays with nardashir has disobeyed Allah and His Messenger."

Aḥmad narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Khaṭmī, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The example of one who plays backgammon (nard) and then stands up to pray is like one who performs ablution with pus and the blood of swine, and then stands up to pray."

Ibn Abī Shaybah and Ibn Abī al-Dunyā narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, who said: "One who plays nard for gambling (qimār) is like one who eats the flesh of swine, and one who plays it without gambling is like one who anoints himself with the fat of swine."

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Kathīr, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by a people playing nard and said: 'Hearts heedless, hands feeble, and tongues idle.'"

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Abī al-Dunyā and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Qatādah, who said: "Al-maysir (gambling game) is qimār."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Abī al-Dunyā, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh narrated through the chain of Layth from ʿAṭāʾ, Ṭāwūs and Mujāhid, who said: "Everything in which there is qimār is of al-maysir, even the children's play with walnuts and knucklebones (kiʿāb)."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Abī al-Dunyā and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Sīrīn, who said: "Qimār is of al-maysir."

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā and Abū al-Shaykh narrated from Yazīd ibn Shurayḥ that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Three things are of al-maysir: whistling to pigeons in the bathhouse, qimār, and striking with knucklebones."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "Al-anṣāb (idols) are stones they used to slaughter for, and al-azlām (divining arrows) are arrows (qidāḥ) they used to seek decisions in matters."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: "They had pebbles; when one of them wanted to raid or to sit down, he would seek a decision by them."

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Mujāhid concerning al-azlām, who said: "They are the knucklebones of Persia with which they gambled, and the arrows of the Arabs."

Many hadiths have been related condemning wine and its drinkers, and the severe warning against it, and that every intoxicant is forbidden. They are recorded in the books of hadith, so we will not prolong the discussion by mentioning them, for that is not our purpose here. Rather, our concern is with what relates to tafsir.
